title: FORD PROJECT:MESSAGE ON SADAT-FORD MEETING
body:
1.  DEPUTY ASSISTANT SECRETARY SOBER PASSED MESSAGE IN
REFTEL TO FORD MIDDLE EAST PRESIDENT WILLIAMS MARCH 31.
WILLIAMS REQUESTED AMBASSADOR'S VIEWS IN CONSIDERING
SUGGESTED MEETING BETWEEN SADAT AND HENRY FORD.  SINCE
WILLIAMS TRAVELING, AMBASSADOR SPOKE WITH WAYNE FREDERICKS
ON APRIL 1 .
2.  ALTHOUGH WE RECOMMENDED THAT FREDERICKS DISCUSS SUG-
GESTED MEETING WITH EGYPTIAN AMBASSADOR GHORBAL IN CONTEXT
THAT IF EGYPTIANS WANTED SUCH A MEETING, FORD WOULD BE
FAVORABLY DISPOSED, FREDERICKS SUBSEQUENTLY CALLED BACK
TO SAY THAT DETROIT (CALDWELL) HAD DECIDED AGAINST AP-
PROACHING GHORBAL.  FORD INCLINED TO WAIT AND SEE WHAT
DEVELOPS FROM EGYPTIAN SIDE DURING SADAT VISIT.
3.  WE HAVE NOT BEEN ASKED TO PASS ANY RESPONSE BACK TO
OUROUSSOFF,   BUT YOU MAY INFORM HIM OF ABOVE FOR
HIS INFORMATION.
VANCE

title: GOK REACTION TO SUSPENSION OF EGYPTIAN-ISRAELI TALKS
body:
1. IN FIRST GOK PUBLIC STATEMENT SINCE SUSPENSION OF
JERUSALEM POLITICAL COMMITTEE TALKS, KUWAIT MINISTER FOR
CABINET AFFAIRS HUSSEIN (IN TALKS WITH NEWSMEN JAN. 20)
REPORTEDLY ATTACKED THE "ISRAELI ENEMY'S" ATTITUDE AS
SHOWING DISDAIN FOR ARAB RIGHTS. THIS DISDAIN, HE ASSERTED,
IS BASED ON US SUPPORT, "WHICH IS IN TURN UNDER PRESSURE BY
ZIONIST PENETRATION IN INFORMATION MEDIA AND ZIONIST PROPAGANDA
WHICH MISLEADS THE AMERICAN PEOPLE." HE CHARACTERIZED
ISRAEL'S GOAL AS "TAKING POSSESSION OF THE RESOURCES OF
THE AREA." HUSSEIN CALLED FOR RESTORATION OF ARAB UNITY
AND REPORTEDLY SAID THAT THE SAUDI FON MIN WILL VISIT
KUWAIT "NEXT WEEK", "FOR CONSIDERATION OF A POSSIBLE
JOINT OR COLLECTIVE MOVE" TO RECONCILE ARAB VIEWS.
2. COMMENT: REPORT OF FORTHCOMING VISIT BY SAUDI FON
MIN CONFLICTS WITH INFORMATION GIVEN TO AMBASSADOR
JAN. 19 BY KUWAITI MFA CHIEF OF PROTOCOL, WHO SAID
THERE WERE NO PLANS FOR SUCH A VISIT.

body:

Sir: I have the honor to enclose a copy of a memorandum addressed on August 23 by the Supreme Allied Commander to the Allied  Control Commission on the subject of its relations with the Italian Government. It will be noted that the Allied Control Commission is instructed to make clear to the Italian Government that its approach to the Allied authorities must be through the Allied Control Commission. The enclosure points out that the Advisory Council for Italy on the other hand is in direct contact with the Allied Control Commission and that the members of the Advisory Council may make joint or several representations to their Governments, but that they are not in direct contact with the Government of Italy.
Respectfully yours,


Robert D. Murphy

title: BRITISH MILITARY AID TO KENYA
body:
1. ACCORDING TO BRITISH HIGH COMMISSION OFFICERS IN NAIROBI,
TURKEY HAS REFUSED BRITISH REQUEST FOR OVERFLIGHT CLEARANCE TO
AIRLIFT URGENTLY NEEDED MUNITIONS TO KENYA. TURKS REPORTEDLY
HAVE TOLD BRITISH THAT THEY SHOULD NOT HAVE DIVULGED PURPOSE
OF AIRLIFT AS THIS MADE IT "ARAB" ISSUE AND TURKEY DOES NOT
WISH TO BE PUT IN POSITION OF KNOWINGLY ANTAGONIZING ARAB
COUNTRIES.
2. OTHER POSSIBLE AIRLIFT ROUTES TO KENYA WERE ALSO EXPLORED
BUT HAVE PROVED INFEASIBLE. WHILE SUDAN GAVE PERMISSION, EGYPT
DID NOT. AIRLIFT FROM ISRAEL VIA SUDAN ALSO PROVED UNWORKABLE
AS BRITISH CONCLUDED IT WOULD BE NECESSARY TO OBTAIN CLEARANCES
FROM JORDAN AND SAUDIA ARABIA IN ORDER TO OVERFLY GULF OF
AQABA.
3. BRITISH AND KENYANS NOW SAID TO BE RESIGNED TO NECESSITY
OF SHIPPING MUNITIONS TO KENYA BY SEA.
MARSHALL

title: President Wilson to the Secretary of State
body:
My Dear Mr. Secretary: I think it would be quite unjustifiable to do anything for the sake of public opinion which might change the whole face of our foreign relations. Therefore I think it would be most unwise to send a message like this.

I had a talk with Walter Page of the most explicit kind, and am sure that he will be able to convey to the powers that be in London a very clear impression of the lamentable and dangerous mistakes they are making. I covered the whole subject matter here dealt with in a way which I am sure left nothing to be desired in the way of explicitness or firmness of tone; and I think that our method had better stop with that for the time being. Let us forget the campaign so far as matters of this sort are concerned.
Faithfully Yours,

W. W.

body:

AND THE DEPUTY POLAD AT SHAPE.  FURTHER CONSIDERATION

RETAIN ALL POLADS.  REGRETTABLY THIS IS NOT POSSIBLE,

SERVICE POSTS.

OPTIMUM SOLUTION.  HOWEVER, FROM CORRESPONDENCE AND DIS-
CUSSIONS WITH AMBASSADOR BREWSTER AND EMBASSY LONDON I AM
CONFIDENT THAT THE VITAL SUPPORT WHICH IS NEEDED CAN BE
PROVIDED.    VANCE

title: The Ambassador in Mexico (Messersmith) to the Secretary of State
body:
A-2709. Reference MacLean's conversation on September 13 with O'Donoghue re increasing total of Mexican workers being repatriated if they were transported by vessel to Tampico.
After discussion of question with competent authorities, Embassy is able to state that Mexican National lines can not handle any number of repatriates in excess of 20,900 monthly. Even though these workers were transported to Tampico or other ports by vessel, they would still have to be brought to interior of Republic and strain on National lines would be same as though they were brought to Mexico via Laredo or El Paso. In other words, equipment and rolling stock directed to Tampico or other ports for purpose indicated would have to be taken from Laredo or El Paso runs with consequent reduction in equipment available for the return of Mexican workers from those ports of entry.


Messersmith

title: The Special Adviser to the President on Foreign Trade (Peek) to the Secretary of State
body:
Dear Mr. Hull: I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of October 1, enclosing a copy of Mr. Flanders' letter of September 26 regarding the financing of an order for machine tools which his company, the Jones & Lamson Machine Company, of Springfield, Vermont, hopes to obtain from the Turkish Government. While the case appears to be of the border line variety, I quite agree that the financing of the proposed transaction by an agency of this Government would be open to serious misconstruction as well as being in conflict with the declared policy of this Government. Accordingly the Export-Import Banks will refrain from participating in any financing which may be involved in the proposed transaction.
I am mailing Mr. Flanders a copy of your letter of October 1 and of my letter of this date for his information.
Very sincerely,
George N. Peek

title: Contacts with member countries: Norway - Corresondence 02
body:
MEMORANDUM FOR THE RECORD
Meeting with Ambassador Sommerfeld of Norway, December 20, 1973
The Ambassador called on Mr. McNamara immediately after signing the
Memorandum of Cooperation between the Bank and Norway. In response to Mr.
McNamara's question, he commented briefly on the political situation in Norway
and said that Mr. Brattele, the present Prime Minister, was likely to command
support from the opposition parties enough to stay in power and conduct sensible
policies, including NATO relations over the near future. This was in contrast to
the situations in Denmark and Sweden where the stability of the Government was
much more precarious.
AL
December 20, 1973

In your performance of this duty, previous instructions will furnish reasons which you will, in your discretion, use to promote the desired solution of the matter.
I am, sir, your obedient servant,

WILLIAM. H. SEWARD.

body:
1960. For Ambassador only. For your personal information Secretary recently discussed Alpha project with President, stating time appeared to have arrived for talk with Nasser, that Alpha contemplated US-UK guarantee borders between Israel and neighboring Arab states and also involved rather heavy financial implications. President indicated he thought it in order for you speak to Nasser on assumption any references to border guarantee or additional financial assistance would be on purely exploratory basis and would avoid any commitment US at this stage.
Following Secretary's return from Europe it is planned discuss Alpha proposals with other interested Department heads and possibly three or four Congressional leaders. Definiteness US undertaking give border guarantee and additional economic and military aid will depend on results these discussions as well as of course on Nasser's initial reactions exploratory talks.
Hoover

body:

1980. SOURCE OF THE TIMES STORY WAS AN UNIDENTIFIED
HIGH LEVEL PAK MILITARY OFFICER IN ISLAMABAD.

TEST SITES, ONE IN SIND DESERT AND THE SECOND IN

ARTICLES.

title: ROK BATTALION COMMANDER BELIEVED KIDNAPPED
body:
1.  ROK MILITARY HAVE INFORMED UNC THEY BELIEVE LT.
COL YU UN HAK AND RADIO OPERATOR REPORTED TO HAVE
DEFECTED TO NORTH KOREA OCTOBER 20 WERE IN FACT PROBABLY
KIDNAPPED.  ROKG NOTES THAT YU'S PROMOTION RECORD AND
PERSONAL LIFE APPEAR TO HAVE BEEN EXEMPLARY,
AND THAT SOME EVIDENCE FOUND IN AREA WHERE YU
WAS LAST SEEN INDICATES THAT FORCE MAY HAVE BEEN EMPLOYED.
UNC ADVISES THEY TENTATIVELY INCLINED TO ACCEPT ROK
ANALYSYS, NOTING THAT RADIO MESSAGES REPORTEDLY SENT
BY YU DURING MOVEMENT TO NORTH MAY IN FACT HAVE BEEN
SENT BY THE NORTH FOLLOWING KIDNAPPING.

FOR PROTEST THROUGH MAC CHANNELS, BUT NONE RECEIVED
AS OF 1800 HOURS OCTOBER 21.
3.  WE WILL PROVIDE MORE COMPLETE DETAILS AS
AVAILABLE AND WILL ADVISE OF ANY REQUEST FOR MAC PROTEST.
SNEIDER

title: 184. Memorandum From James C. Thomson of the National Security Council Staff to the President’s Special Assistant for National Security Affairs (Bundy)
body:
You asked about the genesis of State's new interest in a Laos conference.
The initiative came from Mr. Rusk, who signed off on a circular on May 10th (attached) in which he concluded that since a Cambodia conference was "pretty well out the window", we might turn our attention to a Laos conference in order to maintain some sort of diplomatic track in Southeast Asia.
The responses to this cable have been fairly negative for differing reasons--most cogently, because certain addressee posts disagreed that a Cambodia conference was dead. Since then, as you know, the Cambodia business has shown new signs of life.
State is sending out a new circular today which moves the Laos problem to the back burner and brings the Cambodia one up forward once again.




Jim

body:
IN REPORTING AND COMMENTARY ON SENATE PASSAGE OF MILITARY AID

POLICY AND HAS MADE IT OBLIGATORY FOR THE ADMINISTRATION TO

title: LIBYA COMMUTES PRISON TERMS IN HONOR OF THE NINTH ANNIVERSARY OF THE  LIBYAN REVOLUTION WHICH WILL BE CELEBRATED SEPTEMBER 1, LOCAL MEDIA
body:
IN HONOR OF THE NINTH ANNIVERSARY OF THE LIBYAN REVOLUTION
WHICH WILL BE CELEBRATED SEPTEMBER 1, LOCAL MEDIA ANNOUNCED
AUGUST 30 THAT CIVILIAN AND MILITARY PRISONERS HAVE HAD THEIR
PRISON TERMS REDUCED BY ONE FOURTH. PRISONERS SENTENCED TO
LIFE IMPRISONMENT HAVE HAD THEIR TERMS CHANGED TO FIFTEEN
YEARS IN JAIL. DECISION WAS MADE BY THE GENERAL SECRETARIAT
OF THE GENERAL PEOPLE'S CONGRESS (QADHAFI, JALUD, AND THREE
OTHER OFFICERS) AND IS BELIEVED TO BE THE FIRST GENERAL
COMMUTATION SINCE THE DAYS OF KING IDRIS. AMONG THOSE
APPARENTLY INCLUDED IN THIS RULING ARE THE NUMEROUS
PARTICIPANTS ARRESTED DURING ANTI-GOVERNMENT DEMONSTRATIONS
AT THE UNIVERSITIES IN TRIPOLI AND BENGHAZI IN APRIL 1975.
EAGLETON

title: 114. Memorandum From Secretary of State Vance to President Carter
body:
Zaire. The western ambassadors have begun meetings with Mobutu to urge that he undertake serious reform in Zaire. Giscard called Mobutu to stress the importance of the five-power demarche, and Mobutu received the French Ambassador yesterday. We understand that Mobutu told the French that he agreed with the points made in the five-power memorandum. In response to the French Ambassador's suggestion that relations with Angola be improved, Mobutu said that he was willing to try to reach an understanding with Neto but was skeptical about what could be achieved. Kaunda, he said, has offered to mediate.
Our Ambassador made his demarche today and delivered your letter.
Mobutu read the letter carefully and bristled momentarily at references to corruption, arrests, and executions. His comments were defensive, but he asked that we be assured that he is aware of the need to expedite reform.
[Omitted here are items unrelated to Central Africa.]

title: EFFECT OF PEOPLES COMMITTEES IN CYRENEICA
body:
EMBOFF WHO VISITED CYRENEICA 15-17  JUNE LEARNED IN DISCUSSIONS
WITH SEVERAL EXPATRIATE BUSINESSMEN ( NON- AMERICANS)  THAT
THEIR ATTITUDE TOWARD PEOPLES COMMITTEES WHICH HAVE BEEN
FORMED IN THE PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTOR THERE IS
ESSENTIALLY OPTIMISTIC.   THEY ADMIT THAT,  WHILE ALL
THE RETURNS ARE NOT YET IN,  THERE IS SOME DEGREE OF
CONFUSION REIGNING.   HOWEVER,  EARLY INDICATIONS
ARE THAT THE GREAT MAJORITY OF TENDERS ARE NOW GOING
TO THE LOWEST BIDDERS DUE TO A REDUCTION IN " KICK-
BACK"  ACTIVITY.   TO SOME EXTENT THIS IS DISQUIETING
TO THE EXPATRIATE BUSINESSMEN USED TO DEALING WITH
FAMILIAR " FIVE PERCENTERS",  BUT THERE ARE THOSE WHO
FEEL THAT BUSINESS WILL BECOME MORE REALISTICALLY
COMPETITIVE WITH LESS POLITICS INVOLVED IN THE WINNING
OF CONTRACTS WITH THE LIBYAN GOVERNMENT.
JOSIF

PARENTLY OF A HEART ATTACK JULY 8/9 SLEEPING AT HIS FARM

WILL MEAN FOR THE LIBERAL PARTY AND THE ELECTORAL PROCESS.

BUT HELD NO FORMAL OFFICE OTHER THAN "GENERAL COORDINATOR."
PARADOXICALLY, HIS DEATH MAY MAKE IT EASIER FOR THE LIBERAL
PARTY, CONTROLLED BY RODAS' ADHERENTS, TO UNITE WITH ITS DIS-
SIDENT FACTIONS.
JARAMILLO

title: RHODESIA: SITHOLE AGREES WITH SMITH THAT DEFENSE FORCE SHOULD REMAIN
body:
PRESS ACCOUNTS OF AUGUST 22 REPORT THAT REV. SITHOLE PUBLICLY
BACKED SMITH'S STATEMENT (REFTEL) THAT THE RHODESIAN SECURITY
FORCES SHOULD NOT BE DISBANDED. SITHOLE REPORTEDLY SAID
THAT THE CRUCIAL POINT WAS NOT THEIR DISBANDMENT BUT THEIR
LOYALTY TO THE STATE. HE SAID, "THE PRESENT SECURITY FORCES HAVE
SERVED SUCCESSIVE GOVERNMENTS WITH A PROFESSIONAL LOYALTY
AND WE ARE CONFIDENT THEY WILL CONTINUE TO SERVE THE NEW
GOVERNMENT AND NEW STATE WITH THE SAME LOYALTY." SITHOLE
SAID IT MUST BE REMEMBERED THAT 80 PERCENT OF THE FORCES ARE
BALCK AND THAT BOTH BLACK AND WHITE HAD LONG EXPERIENCE IN
THE FIELD. HE ADDED, "THE SUGGESTION TO DISMANTLE (THEM)
IS NOTHING SHORT OF A PRESCRIPTION FOR CHAOS AND DISORDER. NO SANE
MAN CAN GO ALONG WITH THIS."
EDMONDSON

title: The Under Secretary of State (Welles) to the Lend-Lease Administrator (Stettinius)
body:
My Dear Mr. Stettinius: In view of the efforts which the Turkish Government is now making to prepare for the possible extension of hostilities in the Near East during the spring, the Department of State regards it as particularly important that supplies be furnished to  Turkey as soon as possible, not only for the purpose of strengthening the Turkish Government in its announced determination to resist aggression but also in order to enable that resistance to be effective.
This Department understands that the Turkish military authorities consider it of the greatest importance, for instance, that 950 trucks, for which the Turkish Government has already deposited more than $1,000,000 in cash payment, reach Turkey by the end of March.
Sincerely yours,


Sumner Welles

title: 181. Telegram From the Delegation at the North Atlantic Council Ministerial Meeting to the Department of State
body:
Polto 1759. From USDel. NATO Ministerial Council, meeting in restricted session afternoon December 18, after completing action on defense resolution (reported separately), turned to draft communique. Communique was agreed and text is being transmitted separately.
At conclusion of meeting Secretary expressed appreciation of Council to Spaak for manner in which latter had guided Council's fruitful deliberations. Secretary also thanked International Staff for their  work. Secretary said that spirit of unity displayed by NATO at this Ministerial meeting was best guarantee that peace would continue to be maintained.
Meeting ended at 6 p.m.

body:
1.  IRANIAN CONSULATE GENERAL IN MUNICH WAS TAKEN OVER
LATE LAST WEEK BY GROUP OF IRANIAN STUDENTS, WHO INFORMED

COUNCIL TO OPERATE CONSULATE GENERAL.  CONSUL GENERAL
ASKED POLICE NOT TO INTERVENE, AND PROCEEDED TO ENTER
INTO LENGTHY DISCUSSIONS WITH STUDENTS.  HE MUST HAVE
BEEN EXTREMELY PERSUASIVE, FOR HE WAS ELECTED BY STUDENTS
TO BE MEMBER OF REVOLUTIONARY COUNCIL AND SITUATION IS
NOW CALM.
2.  I TELEPHONED MY IRANIAN COLLEAGUE THIS MORNING.  IT
WAS CLEAR TO ME DURING OUR CONVERSATION THAT ANOTHER
PERSON WAS LISTENING IN AND THAT THE IRANIAN CONSUL
GENERAL WAS GIVING ME A CAREFULLY REHEARSED SPEECH ON
HOW WELL HE AND HIS COLLEAGUES ON THE REVOLUTIONARY
COUNCIL WERE GETTING ALONG.  HENNEMEYER

military police after high school and came up the ranks as Colonel. He
studied political science in University of Mogadishu and University of
Rome in early sixties. In 1964 he was appointed to the post of Director
General in the Ministry of Finance and in 1967 he was promoted as Governor
of the Central Bank. In 1970 he came to Washington as Somali Ambassador
to the U.S. and he kept that post until last month when he was appointed
 
as the new Minister of Finance. As Ambassador, Mr. Addou has worked very
hard and has succeeded in improving U.S.-Somali relations. In addition
to Somali, he speaks English, Italian and some Arabic.

title: The Consul General at Tientsin (Lockhart) to the Secretary of State
body:
Authoritative information just received from Chinwangtao shows that 9 Japanese airplanes bombed for 2 hours this morning front line from Mafeng to Haiyang to north of that town dropping 60 bombs.
Heavy fighting reported at Lulung last night. Responsible Chinese official informed me today that Taitowying has been captured by Japanese. Large number Chinese troops at Changli were withdrawn last night to Lwanchow, according to information received from railway authorities. Request has been received for 40 railway cars at Changli denoting further withdrawal. Present movement is undoubtedly intended to drive Chinese to west bank of Lwan and appears to be succeeding.
Lockhart

title: The Acting Secretary of State to the French Ambassador (Bonnet)
body:
The Acting Secretary of State presents his compliments to His Excellency the Ambassador of France and has the honor to acknowledge the receipt of the Embassy's Note No. 513, of August, 1946, setting forth the views of the French Government on the question of the revision of the Straits Convention. The Department has not failed to take note of the position of the French Government in this matter, and is in full agreement with the latter's view that the problem is one which should be settled at an international conference of all interested powers.
The Ambassador will recall that the Government of the United States, on November 2, 1945, signified its willingness to participate in such a conference; and that this willingness was reaffirmed in the American note to the Soviet Embassy on August 19, 1946, a copy of which was sent to the Embassy of France.

W. J. Bryan

TOGETHER MAY BE UNDER WAY.  ONE ASTUTE DIPLOMAT HERE,

body:
top secret

flash
 
JCS 92985. From JCS to personal for Genl of the Army Douglas MacArthur, SecDef sends. For his eyes only. G. C. Marshall

title: PA APPROVES 1979 BUDGET
body:
1.  FEBRUARY 2 LOCAL PRESS HEADLINES PA "UNANIMOUS APPROVAL"
OF GOE PROGRAMS FOR 1979, INCLUDING BUDGET.  APPROVAL,
WHICH CAME AFTER NINE CONTINUOUS SITTINGS AND STATEMENTS
BY SIXTY SPEAKERS, MARKS A "NEW ERA OF COOPERATION"
BETWEEN THE PA AND THE GOVERNMENT, ACCORDING TO PA
SPEAKER ABU TALEB.  MINPLANNING ABDEL MEGUID, COMMENTING
ON THE DEBATES, TOLD LEGISLATORS THAT EGYPT'S ECONOMY IS
STRONG, WHILE MINFINANCC LOUTTI REASSURED PA THAT ALLOCA-
TIONS FOR ARMED FORCES MAVE BEEN INCREASED UNDER BUDGET
AND SUBSIDIES FOR BASIC COMMODITIES WILL NOT BE TOUCHED.
2.  RESPONDING TO OPPOSITIQN LEADER SHUKRY'S
DEMANDS FOR GOVERNMENT ACTION ON HOUSING PROBLEM,
PM KHALIL STATED THAT HE TOO BELIEVES HOUSING IS EGYPT'S
MOST PRESSING PROBLEM.  HOUSING SHORTAGES, HE INDICATED,
COULD HAVE VERY DANGEROUS SOCIAL CONSEQUENCES.  KHALIL
ENDED BY DECLARING THAT EGYPT "WILL HAVE TO WORK VERY
HARD TO ACHIEVE (ECONOMIC) SUCCESS", AND EXPRESSED
CONFIDENCE EGYPTIANS ARE READY TO UNDERTAKE TASK.  EILTS

title: UN DESERTIFICATION CONFERENCE
body:
AS REQUESTED REFTEL, WE ASKED HEAD OF GREEK DELEGATION TO
DESERTIFICATION CONFERENCE MARINOS YEROLANOS, DEPUTY DIRECTOR
FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROBLEMS IN THE COORDINATION MINISTRY, FOR
HIS VIEWS ON CONFERENCE ISSUES. HE TOLD US HIS DELEGATION IS
UNCOMMITTED ON THE QUESTION OF CONSORTIUM FINANCING.  SINCE
GREECE IS A NET RECIPIENT OF FOREIGN ASSISTANCE, IT DOES NOT
PLAN TO COMMIT RESOURCES FOR FINANCING A WORK PROGRAM, AND
THEREFORE TENDS TO SUPPORT THE US POSITION OPPOSING ADVANCE
TARGETS OR COMMITMENTS FOR A CONSORTIUM.  THE GOG DELEGATION'S
MAIN CONCERN AT THE CONFERENCE IS WITH SCIENTIFIC ASPECTS,
SINCE GREECE MAY BE IN A POSTION TO PROVIDE TECHNICAL
ASSITANCE TO COUNTRIES SUFFERING FROM LOSS OF PRODUCTIVE
CAPACITY THROUGH ENCROACHMENT OF THE DESERT.  THE
DELEGATION WILL THEREFORE INCLUDE EXPERTS FROM THE
AGRICULTURE MINISTRY AS WELL AS COORDINATION AND
FOREIGN MINISTRIES.
MILLS

title: The Chief of the Division of Western European Affairs (Dunn) to the Director of Naval Intelligence, Navy Department (Puleston)
body:
Dear Captain Puleston: Thank you very much for your letter of November 24, 1936, enclosing Lieutenant Commander Gade's report from Brussels.

I found the report most interesting as a clear picture of the official Belgian explanation of its new neutrality policy. Let us not forget, however, that Mr. Van Zeeland's arguments were just as cogent last year or five years ago, but that as long as France held the military supremacy in Europe those arguments were not advanced. I regard Belgium's action, however, as "realistic" policy.
Very sincerely yours,


James Clement Dunn

1.  DEPARTMENT, IN CONSULTATION WITH USIA AND AID, HAS
CAREFULLY EXAMINED EMBASSY'S PROPOSAL TO USE YEMEN

MILITARY OFFICERS.  YALI OPERATES UNDER AUTHORITY OF
UNITED STATES INFORMATION AND EDUCATIONAL EXCHANGE ACT

AUTHORIZE THE PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES RELATED TO THE ...
TRAINING...OF THE ARMED FORCES OF A FOREIGN GOVERNMENT,"
YOUR PROPOSAL IS PRECLUDED BY LAW.  SINCE THIS SECTION
APPLIES TO ACTIVITIES, AS WELL AS TO EXPENDITURE OF FUNDS,
FACT TRAINING WOULD BE REIMBURSED DOES NOT ALTER BASIC PRO-
HIBITION AGAINST PROVIDING IT THROUGH YALI.

title: ETHIO-NIPPON MINING
body:
1. AS A RESULT OF THE ELF ATTACK ON THE DEBAWA SITE OF
ETHIO-NIPPON MINING, ALL OPERATIONS HAVE BEEN SUSPENDED
FOR APPROXIMATELY THREE TO SIX MONTHS. THE MAJORITY OF
THE JAPANESE TECHNICIANS WILL BE LEAVING ASMARA FOR TOKYO
SHORTLY. MANAGERIAL PERSONNEL WILL REMAIN. MR. SUGISAKA,
MANAGER OF THE ASMARA OFFICE, SAID THE ONLY DAMAGE WAS TO
A 600 KILOWATT GENERATOR AND SOME OTHER MACHINERY. ANOTHER
SOURCE REPORTS THAT THE DAMAGE IS ESTIMATED TO BE ONE AND
ONE-HALF BILLION YEN. MR. SUGISAKA INDICATED THAT THE HOME
OFFICE OF NIPPON MINING WILL DECIDE IN THE COMING WEEKS
WHETHER OR NOT TO CONTINUE THEIR OPERATIONS. A DECISION TO
DISCONTINUE OPERAIONS WILL LIKELY CAUSE CONTRACTUAL COMPLICATIONS
WITH THE IEG MINISTRY OF MINES.
PERRY

title: CONGRESSMAN ZABLOCKI IN POLAND
body:
1. ON FRIDAY, U.S. CONGRESSMAN CLEMENT J. ZABLOCKI (DEMOCRAT-
WISCONSIN) CONTINUED HIS CURRENT VISIT IN POLAND WITH A CALL ON
POLISH MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS STEFAN OLSZOWSKI. HE ALSO TOURED

AND TOOK PART IN A RECEPTION AT THE U.S. EMBASSY HONORING AMERICAN
PARTICIPANTS IN THE INTERNATIONAL CHOPIN FESTIVAL.

PERFORMANCE OF THE MOZART REQUIEM MASS AT THE "CHURCH OF THE SACRED
CROSS" ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF FREDERYK CHOPIN'S DEATH. IN THE EVENING,
HE IS THE GUEST OF HONOR AT A RECEPTION HOSTED BY US AMBASSADOR TO
POLAND R. T. DAVIES.
3. ON SATURDAY, THE WISCONSIN CONGRESSMAN LEAVES POLAND AFTER A
FIVE DAY VISIT IN THE COUNTRY.
BRADSHAW

title: The Ambassador in Austria-Hungary (Penfield) to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegram]

 
558. Following my cipher telegram Friday last I can now advise you on high authority that no agreement yet reached with Italy. Conversations in Vienna proceeding at high pressure with all responsible ministers and interested ambassadors. It is admitted Italy has been offered Trentino but makes no promise of continued neutrality. Italy is reported to have received offer from France of Corsica and one half of Tunis as an inducement to join Allies. The German Ambassador assures me Germany contemplates no territorial concessions to Austria as reported. If Trentino ceded to Italy, it will be considered as compensation for some Balkan disappointment of former years. This condition proposed in hopes of swaying Emperor who refuses gratuitously to alienate a province.



Penfield

title: 120. Memorandum From the Secretary of State to the Director of the International Cooperation Administration (Hollister)
body:
I am prepared, with some misgiving, to approve your proposal of May 18, 1956 with reference to ICA responsibility for Public Law 480.
I greatly fear that what I understand to be increased control will be exercised in such a way as to create friction and nullify instead of promote our policy objectives. It is human nature for one human being to enjoy exercising power over another and to seek to extend and enlarge that power. However, I am willing to give this a try.
I believe that reference should be made in your instruction to the supervening circular 58 from the President regarding the responsibility of ambassadors, and that ambassadors should have a responsibility to report if they believe that the procedures in particular  cases are too rigid and are nullifying our foreign policy objectives. In that event, further consideration can be given the matter.
JFD

BELGIANS NOW RETHINKING NATURE AND SCOPE OF THEIR PRO-
POSAL TO ADD AN OBSOLESCENCE CRITERION TO THE COCOM
EMBARGO.  DURING DISCUSSIONS IN BRUSSELS LAST WEEK
BETWEEN UK AND BELGIAN AUTHORITIES ON UK CRITERIA PROPO-

DISCUSSION WITH COMRAS AT COCOM MEETING 3/15, THEY HAD
DECIDED TO REVISE THEIR OBSOLESCENCE PROPOSAL BY ELIMI-
NATING AUTOMATICITY FEATURES.  UNDER REVISED PROPOSAL
UNANIMOUS AGREEMENT WOULD CONTINUE TO BE REQUIRED FOR
THE REMOVAL OF EQUIPMENT FROM THE EMBARGO LIST.  NEVER-
THELESS, THE CRITERION WOULD CREATE A PRESUMPTION THAT
EQUIPMENT COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE IN ANY COCOM MEMBER
COUNTRY FOR OVER FIVE YEARS HAD BECOME OBSOLESCENT.
BELGIANS ARE, ACCORDING TO UK DEL, REDRAFTING THEIR
PROPOSAL AND MAY NOT BE READY TO SUBMIT IT WITHIN NEXT
WEEK AS ORIGINALLY INTENDED.

title: Documentos referentes às relações políticas, econômicas e comerciais entre Brasil e Estados Unidos no período em que Azeredo da Silveira era ministro das Relações Exteriores. O dossiê é constituído de relatórios, notas, discursos, resumos e correspondência, abordando, no âmbito das relações econômicas, a questão da exportação de calçados brasileiros ao mercado norte-americano; a discussão da criação de um grupo consultivo informal Brasil-EUA sobre assuntos econômicos; as questões referentes ao intercâmbio comercial, incluindo as negociações do Acordo Geral de Tarifas e Comércio (GATT), e a lei de comércio norte-americana promulgada em 1975, e que causou polêmica em países da América Latina por desrespeitar acordos firmados anteriormente sobre protecionismo. No âmbito das relações políticas, o dossiê inclui informações relativas ao grupo consultivo Brasil-EUA sobre cooperação científica e tecnológica; sobre a visita de Azeredo da Silveira a Washington, em outubro de 1976; e sobre o projeto e assinatura do Memorandum de Entendimento referente a consultas sobre assuntos de interesse mútuo entre Brasil-EUA. No âmbito dos direitos humanos, inclui informações sobre a prisão política de cidadãos americanos no Brasil, sobre a lei norte-americana de ajuda externa, no campo de segurança e assistência militar; e sobre a denúncia feita pelo governo brasileiro em 1977, do acordo militar Brasil-EUA de 1952.

body:
B. LUSAKA 0960
CAPE TOWN FOR EMBASSY

VISIT REPORTED REF A FROM SAME SOURCE. GROUP ARRIVED MAY 23
AS SCHEDULED BUT FROM DAR RATHER THAN LUSAKA. THEY PROCEEDED
TO ORAPA DIAMOND MINE SAME DAY. FOLLOWING MORNING (MAY 24),
ANGLO-AMERICAN BOARD CHAIRMAN OPPENHEIMER, BOARD MEMBER
J. OGILIVIE THOMPSEON AND HEAD OF "CENTRAL SALES OFFICE" FROM
LONDON MET WITH THEM AT ORAPA.

GENERAL ORIENTATION SPONSORED BY OPPENHEIMER AND HIS DE BEERS
DIAMOND OPERATION. GOVERNMENT OF BOTSWANA WAS NOT DEEPLY
INVOLVED.
3. MINISTER OF MINERAL RESOURCES AND WATER AFFAIRS SEGOKGO
TOLD AMBASSADOR HE MET WITH GROUP BRIEFLY BUT THEY WERE NOT
VERY FORTHCOMING, NOTING THAT VISIT HAD BEEN ARRANGED BY ANGLO-
AMERICAN AND NOT BOTSWANA GOVERNMENT.

title: Mr. Le Ghait to Mr. Gresham.

Mr. Secretary of State: The Belgian Government has received, as the United States Government doubtless has also, a letter from the London International Statistical Institute, advocating a meeting of an international commission for the unification of the systems of admeasuring seagoing vessels that are now in force in the different countries.
My Government would be glad to be acquainted with the views of the United States Government in relation to this proposition. I beg, etc.,
A. Le Ghait.

PUBLIC MEETINGS OF ANY NATURE OTHER THAN THOSE CONVENED TO EX-
PRESS SUPPORT FOR THE 'ETHIOPIA FIRST' MOVEMENT CAN BE HELD WITHOUT

GATHERINGS, MAKING MORE FORCEFUL REITERATION OF WARNING NECES-

DATE. IT REFLECTS CONCERN OVER POSSIBLE REACTION BY CONSERVATIVES
AND FRIENDS OF DETAINED NOTABLES TO TREND OF EVENTS AND ARRESTS.
WE THINK IT ALSO INDICATIVE OF PROPHYLACTIC DESIRE AFCC MINIMIZE
RISKS POSED BY ANY POTENTIAL DISTURBANCES TO WEAKENED CENTRAL
AUTHORITIES (CIVIL AND MILITARY) DURING CURRENT PERIOD OF FLUX.

Memorandum
The American Embassy refers to its memorandum dated December 15, 1937 requesting the Foreign Office to take appropriate action in support of a proposal of the American Ambassador at Hankow to insure the safety of a certain area at Hankow.
The American Embassy now desires to remind the Japanese Government that while the American Government claims absolute freedom for its ships to move and trade on the Yangtze River, the American Government looks to the Japanese authorities to give prior warning in the event of any area on the Yangtze becoming, through steps taken by the Japanese authorities, a danger area.

title: The Ambassador in Chile (Bowers) to the Secretary of State
body:
160. Foreign Office has sent me 9-page aide-memoire deprecating press use of the descriptive term "united and associated American nations." (See Department's 41, January 12.) By juridical argument it seeks to prove (a) that all the adherents to Resolution XV of Habana, having abandoned neutrality for non-belligerency, are in defensive alliance with the American power attacked; (b) that among them no distinction should be made between those which have declared war  and those which have fulfilled their obligations by breaking relations, instituting controls, contributing materials, et cetera; and (c) that the term "associated nations" smacks of Versailles and is outmoded by existing relationship among the American States.
I am forwarding copy by pouch and shall not telegraph text unless so instructed.


Bowers

body:
[Telegram.]

 
482. Your 345, February 22; 351, February 23, 3 p.m.; and 356, February 23, 7 p.m.
Department telegraphing Canada to request Carranza order immediate reconsideration decree as affecting American citizens and to point out injustice of short time limit and unwarrantedly drastic penalties.
Since decree apparently not discriminatory against American citizens and amount of tax seemingly insufficient to be confiscatory, Department does not consider it would be justified in protesting against decree of that character if issued according to law and with reasonable conditions as to compliance.
Please advise American citizens that if called upon to make payment under this decree they should represent to authorities that  matter has been placed before General Carranza with request for reconsideration and ask that pending his decision action be suspended.


Bryan.

body:
.
1.  ARA/CAR DIRECTOR HEWITT CALLED ON BARBADIAN AMBASSADOR
JACKMAN MARCH 30 TO TENDER PAYMENT OF $192,500 IN
FULL INCOMPLETE PAYMENT" OF ALL US OBLIGATIONS CONNECTED
WITH THE NAVFAC ON ITS CLOSURE MARCH 31.  AMBASSADOR
JACKMAN WAS UNCERTAIN ABOUT WHETHER TO ACCEPT THE CHECK OR

NOW REQUESTED RENEWED NEGOTIATIONS, AND BECAUSE THIS
PAYMENT COULD BE CONSTRUED AS THE FINAL ONE.  FINALLY,

REFERENDUM. CHRISTOPHER

body:
No. 631.]

Sir: Your despatch of the 4th of June (No. 424) has been received. I am, sir, your obedient servant,

WILLIAM H. SEWARD.

title: The Chairman of the Trustees of the Transradio Consortium Trust (Davis) to the Assistant Secretary of State (Long)

My Dear Mr. Secretary: I wish to advise you that at the meeting of the Consortium Trustees held this date they approved the action taken by the Brazilian Company in closing its Axis circuits.
On motion of General Harbord the Trustees approved the following policy for the guidance of the Argentine and Chilean Companies:
It is in the interest of all parties concerned that each National Company promptly comply with the wishes of its Government relating to the operation of its international circuits and not hesitate to close any circuit whenever such closure shall be suggested, recommended or ordered by the Government under which it is operating.
Sincerely yours,
Robert C. Davis

title: The Secretary of State to Minister Heimké.
body:
No. 82.]
Sir:I have to acknowledge the receipt of your No. 207 of the 31st ultimo containing a report of your investigation of the murder of William Wright, an American citizen of African descent, at the United Fruit Co.'s banana plantation at Cayuga, on December 15, 1908, by a mob of natives of Guatemala.
You also report that you have formally demanded of the Guatemalan Government the immediate dismissal of Sr. Alberto Garcia from the post of jefe politico at Livingston, as well as the arrest, trial, and punishment of the persons guilty of murdering Wright, and of all the officials through whose failure to act the ends of justice have been thus far frustrated in the present case.
The department approves your course in the matter. You will keep the department advised of the result of your representations to the Guatemalan Government.
I am, etc.,
P. C. Knox.

body:

title: The Minister in Switzerland (Wilson) to the Secretary of State
body:
261. Chaco dispute. Najera approached me today as did subsequently the British Delegation. Najera explained that in a secret meeting of the Council the question had been raised of the shipment of airplanes and motors by the United States which does not appear to have been covered by the embargo. The British Delegation had explained to Najera that they had received a telegram from London reporting a conversation with the Chief of the Latin American Division in Washington in which the British Ambassador was informed that instructions had been given to our customs authorities to "scrutinize"  shipments of airplanes and motors. Both Najera and the British felt that they would be glad if it were possible for a message to be sent through me which I could deliver to Najera to the effect that instructions have been issued to scrutinize carefully such shipments.
Wilson

title: The Ambassador in Japan (Grew) to the Secretary of State
body:
[Extract]
On September 1, Mr. Horinouchi, the Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs, made a radio broadcast to the United States in which he defended Japan's actions in China on the ground of China's anti-Japanese acts and asserted that Japan's intentions were peaceful; stated that the ultimate object of the present hostilities in North China and Shanghai was the realization of a state permitting genuine cooperation between the two countries; and declared that the Japanese expeditionary forces in China had not been sent there for aggressive purposes and that Japan had no territorial designs. Mr. Horinouchi's radio address was similar to speeches subsequently made in the Diet by the Minister for Foreign Affairs and the Prime Minister. Apparently, Mr. Horinouchi's speech received little attention in the United States.

body:
[Telegram.--Paraphrase.]

Mr. Sands reports that former civil governor, Gen. Aris, has sent to ask, through a third person, how he can arrange this matter satisfactorily to the legation, and that the minister for foreign affairs has asked if the legation will accept the removal of Gen. Aris from office and a payment of $1,000 each to Shine and Milliken, and punishment of the policemen who wounded them. Mr. Sands states that the minister for foreign affairs says nothing of the punishment of the aid-de-camp to Gen. Aris who was, according to the testimony submitted to the department, equally guilty. Adds that the minister for foreign affairs is willing to make this settlement immediately, urging that public disgrace is sufficient punishment for Gen. Aris. Mr. Sands asks if the offer shall be accepted, plus the punishment of the General's aide-de-camp.

title: The Consul at Chefoo (Roberts) to the Secretary of State
body:
Referring to my telegram of August 26, 4 p.m., regarding currency situation: 
 The Federal Reserve Bank at Chefoo is withdrawing Chinese national currency from circulation as quickly as possible, creating shortage of currency (old currency).
 The Hong Kong [and] Shanghai Banking Corporation unable to import fresh supplies of Chinese national currency is refusing to purchase bills of exchange covering exports and to fix forward exchange contracts. This measure has been taken to conserve existing stock of bank notes for its depositors. As the Yokohama Specie Bank still adheres to its policy of dealing only in Federal Reserve bank notes at the arbitrary rate of 29 American cents for one dollar Federal Reserve Bank currency, the action of the British Bank increases difficulties of exporters shipping to the United States.
 Federal Reserve bank notes are not accepted in interior of Shantung where export products originate.
 Repeated to Peiping, Chungking.

Roberts

title: 74. Telegram From the White House to the President, at Squaw Island, Massachussets
body:
CAP 63496. Cable to Lodge follows; per Hilsman, Rusk requests you clear this with the President for release.
To Saigon, eyes only for Lodge:
Review of Deptels raises possibility we have not been sufficiently precise in telling you our thoughts about the possible removal of brother Nhu.
From the viewpoint of Vietnamese solidarity and world and domestic US opinion, it is important that Nhu not have a key role.
What we are not yet clear about is whether the step of insisting that he depart the country for an extended period would be necessary to restore the Vietnamese peoples' confidence in their government so as to permit a victory in the war. It is on this point that we hope the reassessment you are now engaged in will shed some light. End of message.

title: 348. Information Memorandum From the President’s Special Assistant (Rostow) to President Johnson
body:
Mr. President:
I forward this working level information on the history of Phantom financing-about which you will no doubt be hearing from Abe Feinberg, etc.
Abe Feinberg came in yesterday to complain again that Clifford is offering only $60 million in credit to the Israelis in a sale of fifty aircraft, whereas the Iranians received $100 million in credit in a sale of thirty-two.

I have reported Feinberg's view to Clifford; but it seems clear that only the President's intervention is likely to alter the Defense Department terms-if you wish to do so.
I pointed out to Feinberg that Eshkol had told you he would be delighted to pay cash on the barrel-head. Abe acknowledges this but says the Israeli foreign exchange position has deteriorated and Israel should not now be treated worse than rich Iran.




Walt

title: The Consul at Harbin (Moser) to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegram]

 
Officially [announced] that Semenov force has advanced to right bank of Onon River. As force nearly doubled by Cossacks, volunteers  will endeavor to cross Onon and hold station of Olovyannaya ninety miles east of Karymskaya [omission] and await there the receipt of further arms from Japan including armored [cars] now en route, also help, before undertaking to advance beyond junction. Has now advanced appliances [headquarters] one mile west of Manchuria [Station] and has requested Chinese Eastern Railway to assume operation of [omission] lines as he advances. Is still receiving money and arms from British and Japanese Governments. His advance has aroused enthusiasm and force is said to have [increased] for past ten days.

Moser

title: STONEHOUSE DECIDES NOT TO RESIGN
body:
1. FUGITIVE MP JOHN STONEHOUSE HAS NOW ADVISED COMMONS
THAT HE DOES NOT WISH TO RESIGN HIS SEAT (REFTEL),
APPARENTLY BECAUSE HE HAS BEEN ADVISED THAT RESIGNATION
WOULD PREJUDICE HIS CHANCES TO REMAIN IN AUSTRALIA.
THE PARLIAMENTARY LABOR PARTY'S (PLP) REACTION TO THIS
DEVELOPMENT HAS BEEN ANGRY, AS HAS THAT OF THE WALSALL
NORTH LABOR PARTY CONSTITUENCY ORGANIZATION.
2. COMMONS LEADER EDWARD SHORT RESPONDED JANUARY 16 BY
CABLING STONEHOUSE FOR AN EXPLANATION OF HIS INTENTIONS.
HE REPORTEDLY HOPES TO HAVE A REPLY BY JANUARY 20.
SHOULD STONEHOUSE REFUSE TO RESIGN, HE CAN BE EXPELLED
BY COMMONS, BUT PRECEDENT REQUIRES THAT THE CASE AGAINST
HIM BE HEARD BY A SPECIAL SELECT COMMITTEE, AND THIS
WOULD ENTAIL CONSIDERABLE TIME.  ACCORDINGLY, THE BY-
ELECTION ANTICIPATED IN REFTEL HAS BEEN DELAYED UNTIL
STONEHOUSE'S SEAT IS VACATED BY RESIGNATION OR EXPULSION.
SPIERS

title: Count Bismarck to Mr. Judd.
body:
The royal government is profoundly moved by the intelligence which reached here yesterday of the assassination of President Lincoln, and the simultaneous attempt on the life of the Secretary of State, Mr. Seward.
In view of the so happily existing friendly relations between Prussia and the United States, the undersigned cannot forbear to express to their government the sincere sympathy of the royal government with the great loss that this crime has inflicted upon them. He therefore requests the envoy extraordinary and minister plenipotentiary of the United States of America, Mr. Judd, that he will convey the expression of these sentiments to his government, and he avails himself of this occasion to renew to Mr. Judd the assurances of his distinguished consideration.

BISMARCK.

Mr. N. B. Judd, &c., &c., &c.

title: DOMEI-HISTADRUT RELATIONS
body:
1.  WHILE ATTENDING ASIAN REGIONAL ORGANIZATION
SPONSORED LABOR SUMMIT IN SINGAPORE LAST WEEK,
DOMEI PRESIDENT AMAIKE AND HISTADRUT GENERAL SECRETARY MICHE
SIGNED AGREEMENT FOR COOPERATION BETWEEN TWO
CONFEDERATIONS.  AGREEMENT PROVIDES FOR ANNUAL
HIGH LEVEL MEETING BETWEEN TWO ORGANIZATIONS
(PRESUMABLY BASED ON MODEL OF AFL-CIO-DOMEI
CONSULTATIONS), WITH AMAIKE ATTENDING FIRST
MEETING IN ISRAEL IN LATTER HALF OF THIS YEAR.
AGREEMENT ALSO SPECIFIES THAT TWO LABOR ORGANIZA-
TIONS WILL INCREASE THEIR ASSISTANCE TO ARO
AFFILIATES IN DEVELOPING NATIONS, INITIALLY BY
ASSIGNING STAFF MEMBERS TO ARO SINGAPORE OFFICE.
ALSO IN AGREEMENT IS EXPRESSION OF HOPE THAT AAFLI
WILL JOIN WITH DOMEI AND HISTADRUT IN VARIOUS
LABOR EDUCATION AND DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS.  IN
THIS CONNECTION, WE UNDERSTAND FROM DOMEI HEAD-
QUARTERS THAT HISTADRUT MAY INVITE AAFLI DIRECTOR
PALADINO TO ATTEND MEETING WITH DOMEI IN ISRAEL.
MANSFIELD

title: The Acting Director General of the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration (Hendrickson) to the Secretary of State
body:
Sir: With reference to this Administration's note of 4 October 1944, I am pleased to acknowledge the receipt of the Department's communication, dated 13 November 1944, conveying the comments of the Government of the United States with regard to the two draft Sanitary Conventions which were approved in principle by the Council at its Second Session.
The comments were given careful consideration on 5 December 1944 by a Subcommittee on Draft Conventions, which was appointed by the Standing Technical Committee on Health. On 9 December 1944 the Subcommittee presented revised drafts of the International Sanitary Convention, 1944, and the International Sanitary Convention for Aerial Navigation, 1944, before the Standing Technical Committee on Health. Final drafts of the Conventions were adopted by unanimous vote of that Committee. The English language texts of these Conventions were transmitted to the Department on 14 December 1944.

Accept [etc.]


Roy F. Hendrickson

title: Lord Lyons to Mr. Seward.
body:
Sir: Complaints having been made to her Majesty's consulate at New York that several British subjects had been illegally enlisted into the United States  naval service, and were on board the receiving-ship North Carolina, the acting consul sent recently one of his clerks with a written request to Admiral Paulding for permission to have access to these men, but the permission was refused.
As it is naturally of importance that the acting consul, before bringing these matters before the legation, should be enabled to elicit all the facts bearing upon them, I shall feel obliged if permission could be granted to him to visit, either in person or by deputy, the receiving-ship whenever the nature of the case may require it.
I have the honor to be, with the highest consideration, sir, your most obedient, humble servant,

LYONS.
Hon. William H. Seward,
&c., &c., &c.

body:
No. 605.]
Sir: I have to acknowledge the receipt of your dispatch No. 1181 of the 13th ultimo, reporting a conversation that you had on the 8th ultimo with Mr. Mariscal in relation to the claim of the Roman Catholic Church of California against Mexico growing out of the Pious fund of the Californias.
Your action in the matter is approved by the Department.
The stipulations or terms of the arbitration agreement, as well as the name or names of the arbitrator or arbitrators to be appointed, should be submitted to the Department for approval in advance.

I am, sir, etc.,
John Hay.

According to a memorandum of a telephone conversation on February 24, 1965, between President Johnson and Assistant Secretary of State for Inter-American Affairs Thomas Mann, the following discussion took place:

This is to notify you of the above.

body:
1.  FOREIGN MINISTRY HAS ANNOUNCED THAT PROMINENT
LAWYER JORGE SAMPAIO AND ECONOMIC PLANNER JOAO
CRAVINHO WILL UNDERTAKE SPECIAL MISSION TO US WITHIN
FEW DAYS TO EXPLAIN NEW PORTUGUESE POLICIES AND CARRY

title: The Secretary of State to the Ambassador in Cuba (Judah)
body:
54. Your despatch No. 655, May 7, 1929, regarding Harrah claim. Since the statement of the Cuban Secretary of State to you on May 7, that his suggestions regarding the form of the arbitral agreement would be sent to you within a day or two, Department does not understand why they have not been forthcoming. The proposed agreement has been before the foreign office since March 11. Department had expected that once arbitration was agreed upon the setting up of the arbitral machinery would be expedited. The financial distress experienced by the claimant as a result of the destruction of his property is being accentuated by the continued delay in affording him a remedy.
Please take up matted at once with foreign office in the sense of the foregoing and insist that it be given prompt attention.
Stimson

PARTICIPANTS REGARDING AGENCY AGREEMENTS AND ACTUAL

SURVEY OF SUBJECT EXHIBITION.  IF NOT, WOULD COMMERCE HAVE ANY
OBJECTION TO EMBASSY SENDING CIRCULAR LETTER TO THE 232 PARTICIPATING

WOULD OF COURSE BE PROVIDED TO COMMERCE.  EMBASSY HAS SUFFICIENT

title: The Chargé in Paraguay (Trueblood) to the Secretary of State
body:
confidential

us urgent
 
341. Negrao de Lima returned here yesterday. He tells me rebels will not accept government's terms of unconditional surrender, feeling that they can prolong struggle indefinitely and eventually win. Rebels will accept, however, following terms: 
Free elections guaranteed by either non-partisan or coalition government, Morinigo to finish out his term, and armed forces to be reorganized on basis of professional officers, which will in turn guarantee government.

Negrao feels situation has changed radically since he was last here with government now faced by 4-6-month struggle to defeat rebels, whereas earlier they spoke of an end by June 15, etc.
He is conferring now with Foreign Minister.
Sent Department 341; repeated Rio 66, Buenos Aires 100.


Trueblood

body:
My Dear Doctor Mezes: I submitted your diagram of the proposed personnel for the peace conference to the President after Cabinet meeting on Tuesday, the 29th. After a very brief discussion of it I left it with him for his consideration. This morning he returned the diagram to me with a letter a copy of which I enclose.

I think it would be very well, therefore, after you have thought the matter over, to arrange to come here and see me. Possibly you could do so early next week. Meanwhile I will endeavor to work out the organization in accordance with the President's suggestion from the Department's standpoint.
Very sincerely yours,



Robert Lansing

title: The Chargé in Finland (McClintock) to the Secretary of State
body:
784. The Swiss Minister last night told me he and his wife had lunched alone with President and Mrs. Ryti on June 1. Mr. Egger said he had asked the President about relations with the United States. Ryti replied that Finland could do nothing; that its fate rested with the decision of the great powers. As for the United States it might,  if it wanted to please the Russians, acquiesce in the USSR doing what it wished with Finland. The President concluded by saying "The Americans have offered us only words. The Germans have given us bread". In this brief description you have a precisely accurate picture of the frame of mind which now dominates the makers of policy in this country.


McClintock

title: The United States Political Adviser for Germany (Murphy) to the Secretary of State
body:
confidential 
2922. Reurcirtel Nov 7, 1946, 4 p.m. on restitution Danube craft. Restitution proceeding satisfactorily in atmosphere of cordiality between Hungarians, Yugoslavs and Czechs and OMG authorities. To date 184 Hungarian, 162 Yugoslav, and 25 Czech have been restituted, which number represents all non-controversial claims. Twenty-four Hungarian craft, 17 Yugoslav craft presently retained pending clarification titles. Friendly and understanding atmosphere prevails with respect to these craft. Twenty-five Rumanian and 3 Greek craft still retained due to fact that no mission has arrived. Twenty-eight French and 8 Belgian craft in process of restitution. Nonriparian states owning craft are negotiating with riparian states in some instances for sale of craft. Craft are proceeding downstream to home countries. However, movements seriously impeded due to low water and channel obstructions. To date 33 Hungarian craft and 34 Yugoslav craft have departed from Germany.
Murphy

title: The Chargé in Bolivia (Hibbard) to the Secretary of State
body:
37. My telegram No. 36, June 20, noon. The situation in La Paz and throughout the country remains very tense. Last night an attempt against the Government here, including plans for Siles' assassination, was frustrated. There were street demonstrations last night and this morning. In the latter two students agitating against the Government were killed. There is no doubt that the Government exaggerates these demonstrations for the purpose of putting on heavier military restrictions but the situation is serious and there may be grave trouble before the elections next Sunday, particularly as those opposed to the Government are lining up with Communist elements.
Hibbard

title: LESOTHO NOT SNUBBING BOTSWANA
body:
1. RAND DAILY MAIL ISSUE OF JULY 22 REPORTED THAT GOL
HAS DELIBERATELY SNUBBED BOTSWANA BY HAVING KING
MOSHOESHOE II ACCEPT INVITATION TO VISIT LIBERIA INSTEAD
OF BOTSWANA ALTHOUGH KING HAD EARLIER OUTSTANDING
INVITATION FROM PRESIDENT KHAMA. SNUB REPORTEDLY GIVEN
BECAUSE OF GOL UNHAPPINESS OVER LESOTHO POLITICAL
REFUGEES SHELTERING IN BOTSWANA.

FOR REPORT. KING'S VISIT TO LIBERIA WAS TIMED TO COINCIDE
WITH THAT COUNTRY'S NATIONAL DAY CELEBRATIONS AND HE
MAY WELL VISIT BOTSWANA LATER. GOL PROBABLY WAS
SLIGHTLY UPSET THAT IN WAKE OF 1974 COUP THAT SOME
POLITICAL REFUGEES (GOL CALLS THEM CRIMINAL FUGITIVES)
MADE THEIR WAY TO OR THROUGH BOTSWANA, BUT THERE ARE
NO CONVINCING INDICATIONS THAT LESOTHO/BOTSWANA RELATIONS
WERE UNSETTLED AS A RESULT.
HAUGHT

title: The Ambassador in Spain ( Willard) to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegram]

 
1743. Late yesterday afternoon Prime Minister summoned all Ministers, diplomats absent to come to Madrid immediately for council to be held there today. They declined to give any information as to reason for this sudden meeting. Embassy has just learned that Spanish ship Carasa which left Bilbao for Cardiff with cargo of minerals on August 19, has been torpedoed. Six victims, no further details known at present. News of first sinking doubtless known to Spanish Government yesterday and was reason for council. In view of recent Spanish note to Germany (1708, August 22, 2 p.m., and 1725, August 29 [25], 10 a.m.), a very grave situation has arisen.



Willard

title: Mr. Conger to Mr. Hay.
body:
[Telegram.--Paraphrase.]

(Mr. Conger reports that a conference was held on the 5th instant by the foreign ministers with the Chinese plenipotentiaries, who presented the difficulties in the way of executing Prince Tuan, Duke Lan, and Tung Fu-hsiang. They promise death of Chuang and Yu Hsien, but urge leniency for the others, and beg that they and the court be not placed in too difficult a position. Subsequently the foreign ministers agreed to demand capital sentence, to be immediately commuted to exile, for Tuan and Lan, and death penalty for the others mentioned in the decree, adding Yu Hsien, Chi Hsiu, and Hsu Cheng-yu, the two latter being now prisoners of the Japanese in Peking. Posthumous honors for the members of the Tsungli Yamen, executed last summer, are also to be demanded.)

body:
1038. Sun Fo who returned to Paris recently from Moscow said to me that his negotiations in Moscow had been most successful. The Soviet Government had promised to continue to supply China with arms and munitions on credit. He asserted that six Japanese divisions had lost all their heavy artillery and tanks as a result of the Yellow River inundations. Bullitt

title: WESTERN SAHARA: ARMS OFFER TO MOROCCO
body:
-            --
CHRIS:  I'VE JUST READ THE BRIEFING PAPER FOR YOUR TALK
WITH HASSAN ABOUT THE WESTERN SAHARA.  I AM STRUCK BY THE
EXTENT TO WHICH THE CONDITIONALITY OF THE ARMS OFFER,
WHICH SEEMED QUITE CLEAR IN THE WHITE HOUSE DOCUMENT,HAS
BEEN FUZZED IN YOUR TALKING POINTS.  IN MY OPINION THE
PROPOSED APPROACH FAILS TO MAKE EFFECTIVE USE OF THE
LEVERAGE AFFORDED BY THE PRESIDENT'S DIFFICULT DECISION.IT
GUARANTEES FUTURE TROUBLE WITH HASSAN AND THE CONGRESS
BY FAILING TO MAKE IT CLEAR TO HASSAN FROM THE OUTSET THAT
WE EXPECT HIM TO DEAL IF HE GETS THE ARMS. ALSO, I AM
TROUBLED BY POINTING OUT TO HASSAN THAT "THE U.S. HAS
AVOIDED FORMAL DEALINGS WITH THE POLISARIO..." THIS
IS ONLY A STEP AWAY FROM A COMMITMENT SIMILAR TO ONE
WHICH HAUNTS US IN THE PALESTINE QUESTION.  VANCE

title: ASSISTANCE TO LDC OIL BUYERS
body:
1.  AT A JANUARY 11 PRESIDENTIAL RECEPTION FOR CHIEFS OF
MISSION, PRESIDENT ODUBER TOLD CHARGE THAT VENEZUELA HAS
AGREED TO CONTRIBUTE $100 MILLION TO OPEC'S $1 BILLION LOAN
FUND FOR LDCS.  HE SAID THAT LDC PURCHASERS OF VENEZUELAN
PETROLEUM WOULD BE ABLE TO DRAW ONNBHIS FUND TO THE EXTENT OF
10 PER CENT OF THE AMOUNT OF THEIR ANNUAL PETROLEUM PURCHASES.
THE TERMS WOULD BE 2 PER CENT AND 30 YEARS AND THERE WOULD BE
NO RESTRUCTIONS ON USE OF THE FUNDS.   ODUBER STATED THAT HE
REGARDED THIS ARRANGEMENT AS MUCH MORE BENEFICIAL TO COSTA
RICA THAN THE PUERTO ORDAZ ARRANGEMENT.
2.  THE EMBASSY IS NOT CERTAIN HOW MUCH CREDENCE TO ATTACH
TO THE DETAILS OF THIS REPORT IN VIEW OF PRESIDENT ODUBER'S
RECENT MISSTATEMENT OF VENEZUELA'S INTENTION RE PREFERENTIAL
OIL PRICE FOR CENTRAL AMERICAN COUNTRIES.  KILDAY

title: Mr. Egan to Mr. Blaine.
body:
[Telegram.]

Mr. Egan states that no reply had yet been received to his protest. During the last two days twenty persons, some of whom were Americans, had been arrested for entering the legation, and others had been  prevented from entering by warning of the police. All this is intended to force him to drive out refugees, which, he states, he will not do without instructions. He has addressed a second note to the minister for foreign affairs requesting [an explanation of] such very extraordinary, unjustifiable, and offensive conduct, which is strongly condemned by a large majority of the serious public men.

title: The Acting Secretary of State to the British Ambassador.
body:
My Dear Mr. Ambassador: With reference to your note of May 7, 1904, in which you informed Mr. Hay that you had been so good as to forward to the secretary of state for foreign affairs and the governor-general of Canada copies of Mr. Hay's note and its inclosures regarding the scheme to prevent the destruction of Niagara Falls by the use of its waters by manufactures, I venture to bring the matter to your attention again.
The Department is in daily receipt of letters of inquiry on this subject from anxious correspondents, many from persons of high standing and importance, and would be glad to tell them that there is hopeful progress toward a mutually beneficial understanding in this regard.
I am, etc.,
F. B. Loomis.

ACADEMY OF SCIENCES - NATIONAL ACADEMY OF ENGINEERING.

PRESIDENT KHAMA
PLEASE CONVEY FOLLOWING PERSONAL MESSAGE TO PRESIDENT
KHAMA FROM SECRETARY KISSINGER.  QUOTE:  DEAR MR. PRESI-
DENT:  AS I PREPARE TO RELINQUISH MY DUTIES, I WOULD
LIKE TO EXTEND MY SINCERE THANKS TO YOU AND YOUR ADVISORS
FOR THE COOPERATION YOU HAVE SHOWN AS WE HAVE WORKED
TOGETHER ON THE IMPORTANT ISSUES OF SOUTHERN AFRICA.  I

title: POSSIBLE POSTPONEMENT OF OPEC MEETING IN CARACAS TO PRESERVE OPEC  UNITY
body:
1.  UPON HIS RETURN FROM TRIP TO GULF OPEC CAPITALS,IR
UAE OIL MINISTER UTAYBA ANNOUNCED THAT AMONG COUNTRIES
HE HAD VISITED, SOME WANTED PRESERVE OPEC UNITY. UTAYBA
SAID THAT UAE POSITION WAS THAT CARACAS OPEC CONFERENCE
SHOULD TAKE PLACE AS SCHEDULED. HOWEVER, IF
THERE IS NO UNIFIED DECISION ON PRICES BEFORE
OPEC CONFERENCE CONVENES, THEN THE ISSUE
SHOULD BE SETTLED BY AN EMERGENCY MEETING TO
BE HELD AFTER THREE MONTHS. THIS EXTRA TIME
WOULD GIVE OPEC COUNTRIES A CHANCE TO REACH AN
AGREEMENT AND PRESERVE OPEC UNITY.
DA2.  COMMENT: UTAYBA IS BRIEFING SHAIKH ZAYID
ON HIS MEETINGS AND I EXPECT TO SEE UTAYBA SOON.
HOWEVER, I AM TOLD IN MEANTIME THAT UAE THINKING NOW IS
TO POSTPONE OPEC MEETING FOR AT LEAST THREE
MONTHS THEREBY EXPENDING PRICE FREEZE DURING
THAT PERIOD.
DICKMAN

No. 1354.]

I have the honor to be, sir, your obedient servant,

title: The Under Secretary of State (Welles) to the Under Secretary of War (Patterson)
body:
My Dear Mr. Secretary: I enclose for your information a copy of despatch no. 159 of February 24, 1943, received in this Department from the American Consul at Para, Brazil recommending the withdrawal of the United States Army detachment at Manaos, Brazil. There are also enclosed paraphrases of telegrams exchanged between the Department of State and the American Ambassador at Bio de Janeiro on this subject.
In the light of the comment made by Ambassador Caffery in his telegram no. 1438, March 23, concerning the continued presence in Manaos of this Army detachment, I believe that you may wish to investigate the desirability of assigning this unit to other duty. I should appreciate being informed of any action taken by the War Department in this regard.
Believe me,
Sincerely yours,
Sumner Welles

title: TORONTO STOCK BROKER FEARS WEAKENING OF GENERAL CANADIAN SHARES  FOLLOWING QUEBEC ELECTIONS
body:
1. A VERY CLOSE AND RELIABLE CONTACT WITH DOMINION SECURITIES
HARRIS, TORONTO, TOLD ME NOVEMBER 18 THAT SELLING WAVE OF
STOCKS IN QUEBEC AND OF SHARES IN QUEBEC-BASED FIRMS ACCOMPANIED
BY A GENERAL CANADAIN SELLING TREND HE CHARACTERIZED AS "SELLING
CANADA." HE SAID THAT NEITHER HE NOR HIS ASSOCIATES COULD
UNDERSTAND, FOR EXAMPLE, WHY BROKERAGE RECEIVING SIGNIFICANT
NUMBER SELLING ORDERS FOR CALGARY POWER. HE ATTRIBUTED THIS
TO "SELLING CANADA" TREND -- NOT YET TO DANGEROUS LEVELS, IN
HIS OPINION, BUT SOMETHING TO WATCH.
2. HE CHARACTERIZED THIS WEEK IN THE MARKET AS EXTENSIVE SELLING
BY MAN IN THE STREET JOINED ON WEDNESDAY BY INSTITUTIONAL
SELLING WITH BOTH CONTINUING. HE ATTRIBUTED THE CURRENT
MARKET DEPRESSION DIRECTLY TO THE QUEBEC ELECTIONS. HE
TOLD ME THAT AS OF THURSDAY MORNING BLUE CHIPS WERE FIRMING
UP ACROSS CANADA, ALTHOUGH SITUATION STILL UNSETTLED IN
QUEBEC.

body:
1.  SOVIET WRITER MRS. LYUDMILLA KUZNETSOVA WAS DENIED ENTRY TO
US EMBASSY SHORTLY AFTER 6 P.M. MOSCOW TIME APRIL 18 BY UNIFORMED
MILITIA ON DUTY OUTSIDE EMBASSY.  MS. KUZNETSOVA, A LONG-

HAD BEEN THEIR GUEST DURING A SHOWING OF THE FILM DR. ZHIVAGO.
CONSOFFS ASKED MILITIA REASON FOR BARRING ENTRY AND RECEIVED REPLY

TODAY UNQUOTE.

UNHINDERED, AFTER ASCERTAINING THAT MILITIA HAD NOT SIMPLY MADE
MISTAKE, BUT WERE ACTING UNDER ORDERS.
3.  EMBASSY INTENDS PROTEST DENIAL OF ACCESS, WHICH MAY BE TIED TO
SOVIET PROTEST AND OUR RESPONSE ON INVITING SOVIET CITIZENS
TO FILM SHOWING OF DOCTOR ZHIVAGO AND GIRL FROM PETROVKA (REFTEL).

title: 155. Memorandum From the President’s Staff Secretary (Goodpaster) to the President’s Special Assistant for National Security Affairs (Jackson)
body:
During his meeting with you and Governor Stassen today, the President indicated that, on further reflection, he had come to the rather clear view that the United States could not undertake disarmament or restriction of armaments in any major fields (other than small test or laboratory-type projects) without assured provision for aerial inspection.
Governor Stassen commented that we could move progressively into the field of aerial inspection, and could delay reduction in armaments until aerial inspection is initiated. The President thought his earlier statement would apply to "any disarmament move."
With the qualification of this later conclusion of the President, he indicated agreement with your record of last Tuesday's meeting.
A.J. GoodpasterColonel, CE, US Army

title: The Secretary of State to the Minister in Greece (MacVeagh)
body:
59. Your No. 72, February 12, 2 p.m. The Prime Minister's appeal is, of course, receiving our earnest and sympathetic consideration. You may inform him that the so-called Lend-Lease Bill now before the Congress and which has been passed by the House of Representatives and by the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate, permits in its present form the President to supply the materials of war to those nations which are now the victims of aggression or which are threatened with aggression.
Steps are being taken to create an organization to consider requests for such materials, and the needs of Greece, which have been brought to our attention by the Greek Government, will be referred to that organization.


Hull

title: SCANDINAVIANS PREPARED TO PROVIDE UN PEACE-KEEPING FORCE FOR  MIDDLE-EAST
body:
FORCE FOR MIDDLE-EAST
1. NORWEGIAN DEFENSE MINISTER FOSTERVOLL HAS STATED THAT NORWAY,
SWEDEN, DENMARK AND FINLAND ARE PREPARED TO PROVIDE A 4-POWER,
5,200 MAN PEACE KEEPING FORCE FOR SERVICE IN THE MIDDLE EAST IF
REQUESTED BY THE UNITED NATIONS. DEFENSE MINISTER MADE
STATEMENT DURING NATIONALLY BROADCAST RADIO INTERVIEW
FOLLOWING OCT 17-18 MEETING OF NORDIC DEFENSE MINISTERS AT
ROROS, IN CENTRAL NORWAY.
2. MINISTERS WERE BRIEFED ON CURRENT SITUATION IN MIDDLE EAST
AND EXPRESSED CONCERN OVER POSSIBILITY OF ESCALATION OF CRISIS.
ACCORDING TO PRESS REPORTS, NORWAY WOULD CONTRIBUTE 1290 MEN
AND 4-POWER FORCE COULD BE READY TO DEPART 6 DAYS FOLLOWING
NOTIFICATION TO RESPECTIVE COUNTRIES.
3. COMMENT. ACCORDING TO EMBASSY CONTACT IN DEFENSE MINISTRY,
ROROS MEETING WAS OTHERWISE QUITE UNEVENTFUL. SOURCE ADDED
THAT NECESSARY STAFF WORK AND COORDINATION INCLUDING JOINT
TRAINING FOR 4-POWER FORCE HAD BEEN COMPLETED AND PEACE KEEPING
UNIT WAS IN HIGH STATE OF READINESS.  BYRNE  UNQUOTE  RUSH

title: The Consul General at Jerusalem (Knabenshue) to the Secretary of State
body:
Continued disturbances Jerusalem and vicinity last night. Numerous casualties. One synagogue and several homes burned. Three aeroplanes circled Jerusalem this morning disbursing [dispersing] with machine gun fire approaching bands of Moslem villagers. About 50 British troops arrived by aeroplanes last evening from Egypt and 600 by train this afternoon, which is expected to improve the situation in Jerusalem tonight. Americans who took refuge in the consulate general last night returned to homes today.
Total casualties to date estimated at about 100 killed and more than 300 wounded.
Telaviv today attacked by Moslems from Jaffa but the timely arrival of British troops reported to have saved the situation and British war vessel is expected to arrive there tomorrow. Disturbances reported to have commenced in other sections of the country.
Knabenshue

852. Following from Reuter, Shanghai, September 25th: 
"Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang, interviewed by a representative of the North China Daily News at Mukden, stated that his intention was vigorously to maintain the integrity of the customs and to secure that service from military interference.
He added: I have telegraphed to the Inspector General of Customs to take full control and to appoint his own commissioner and staff at Tientsin.
Marshal Chang announced that he was assuming control in North China for the purpose of protecting that region. His intervention he said had been delayed owing to the necessity of first arranging details with Nanking. He was working for an early cessation of hostilities  [in the] hope that with peace Nanking would take the necessary steps to inaugurate changes satisfactory to all classes and all shades of political opinion."

For the Minister:Perkins

title: Memorandum by the Acting Secretary of State
body:
The Belgian Ambassador came in to ask certain questions regarding our reply to his note indicating that the Belgian Government was unable to pay the June 15th instalment. He could not understand certain points of the note, which Mr. Moley and I explained to him. He asked whether there was any possibility of conversations with Belgium on the debt question during the summer months. He was told that, as far as we know, he was entirely free this summer and that  there was no plan as yet to discuss the debt problem with those countries which had not paid anything on their instalments due. The Ambassador seemed quite happy because he felt free to go home and take his summer holiday as planned.


William Phillips

(Here quote Telegram No. 46, April 21, 5 p.m., from Bogota)
The "Lester Formula" referred to therein was proposed by the League Advisory Committee on Leticia and proved inacceptable to Colombia partly because it was not so worded as explicitly to confirm Colombian sovereignty over Leticia and partly because it did not specifically provide that the "international forces" to be employed by the League Commission should be Colombian forces.
The Department considers that this new Colombian proposal modifying the Lester Formula offers an eminently fair and reasonable solution and desires that you so inform the Foreign Office expressing the hope that the British Government will urge its acceptance at Geneva.

body:
397. Embassy's 395, September 7 [6], 8 [9] p.m. Dr. Melo who has been apprised by the press of the denial issued by the White House has requested that the following message of clarification be transmitted to the President.
Dr. Melo asserts that at no time during the course of his speech yesterday did he say that President Roosevelt told him that the Senate would ratify the sanitary convention. On the contrary the President has explained to him that this was a time of political unrest and therefore not a suitable one to raise such an issue. Once this time were past, however, he (the President) had felt that an equitable solution could be reached.
Tuck

title: RIOTING IN MOSLEM AREA OF CALCUTTA
body:
1. THERE WAS RIOTING IN MOSLEM QUARTER OF CALCUTTA,
IN NORTH/CENTRAL AREA OF THE CITY, THIS MORNING

INJURED. STORY THAT WE HAVE AS OF THIS MOMENT IS
THAT POLICE STARTED DETAINING TICKETLESS RAIL
TRAVELERS AT A RAIL STATION, RIOTING BROKE OUT AND
THE POLICE FIRED INTO THE CROWD.
2. SCHOOLS IN THE AREA HAVE CLOSED AND APPARENTLY
THERE IS CONSIDERABLE TENSION.
KORN
UNQUOTE

title: The Minister in Liberia (Walton) to the Secretary of State
body:
47. For McBride. Japanese Government and a Dutch syndicate are negotiating with Liberian Government concessions to develop Republic's rich iron deposits. Proposals contemplate building railroads and harbors.
Manager of Dutch diamond syndicate which is operating here returned last week from Europe; he has opened negotiations on behalf of his nationals. A representative clothed with power to make definite and specific commitments is expected to arrive on the next Dutch vessel January 15.
In his absence Barclay has delegated Secretary of the Treasury Dennis to engage in preliminary discussions. Practicability of Liberian Government granting concessions to both applicants, allocating mineral land in different sections of the country, is under consideration.
Walton

title: CONTINUING JAPANESE INTERESTS IN POSSIBLE UN OPERATIONS IN SOUTHERN  AFRICA
body:
SOUTHERN AFRICA
1.  GAIMUSHO UN POLITICAL AFFAIRS DIRECTOR MAKOTO WATANABE
IN CONVERSATION ON A NUMBER OF SUBJECTS WITH POLCON NOVEMBER
30, TALKED ON JAPAN'S CONTINUING INTEREST IN THE DEVELOPMENT
OF THE NEGOTIATION EFFORTS IN ZIMBABWE AND NAMIBIA.  AFTER
RECEIVING A GENERAL BRIEFING ON THE STATUS OF THOSE WESTERN
EFFORTS, WATANABE ASKED ABOUT THE PROSPECTS FOR REQUIREMENT FOR
UN PEACEKEEPING AND POLITICAL OBSERVER FORCES IN THE TWO
AREAS.  HE SAID TOKYO CONTINUES TO BE INTERESTED IN THE
POSSIBILITY THAT JAPAN COULD MAKE A CONTRIBUTION IN SUCH A
UN OPERATION.  WHILE STRICTLY MILITARY FUNCTIONS DO NOT
APPEAR TO BE CONSTITUTIONALLY OR POLITICALLY FEASIBLE,
PARTICIPATION IN A FORCE DESIGNED TO PERFORM CIVIL POLITICAL
OBSERVATION OR ADMINISTRATIVE FUNCTIONS MIGHT PERMIT JAPANESE
PARTICIPATION.
YOUNG

My August 17, 1 [3?] p.m. and subsequent mail despatches.

title: The Secretary of State to the Chargé in China (Mayer)
body:
[Paraphrase]

80. For Minister and Charge: Withdrawal of the three cruisers now on China station is recommended by Navy Department.
As to advisability of withdrawing any of cruisers at this time, Department wishes your confidential opinion and, if you consider it wise, also that of the consul general at Shanghai, and any others with whom you may desire to consult.
According to our information, the forces of Great Britain in China are being reduced, but it appears that War and Navy Departments are differently informed in regard to actual number of British forces. The British forces number 4,500 men, according to Navy information, but number 7,222 according to War information. It is desired that you ascertain the correct number and inform the Department.
In order to enable us to reach a decision, the above information is necessary in addition to that contained in Legation's 135, March 2, 4 p.m.

title: The Consul General at Sydney (Moffat) to the Secretary of State
body:
The Prime Minister has now indicated that he will present to Parliament Friday afternoon or evening an amending tariff schedule designed to correct to some extent the adverse balance of trade with America. The new duties will become effective as soon as tabled but must be validated by Parliament within 6 months in order not to lapse. Although the new schedule is a closely guarded secret the best opinion available is that the "general tariff" rather will be substantially increased on a selected list of items of which we are the predominant supplier, with emphasis on luxury and semi-luxury products.
Throughout the past 6 weeks editorial opinion has continued to caution against action directed exclusively at our trade; the Government's  supporters in Parliament on the other hand have been almost unanimous in pressing Lyons to take drastic action.


Moffat

title: Colonel E. M. House to the Secretary of State
body:
Dear Mr. Lansing: Bernstorff has just left. He told me of his interview with you yesterday.
I am glad you have taken this action for the country will sustain you. Bernstorff was anxious that you should not make the announcement for a few days and he was also anxious that you should make it clear that he was in no way involved mentioning him by name. He thinks if this is not done there will be a hue and cry in the press to have him also go.
Would it not be well to make the announcement on Monday and let it come out with the President's message?
I think it is due Bernstorff to help him out where possible. For the first time, he seemed nervous and excited, although as usual he was temperate in his speech and blamed no one.
Sincerely yours,


E. M. House

John Hay.

title: JPNARAYAN\'S HEALTH
body:
1. AFTER RUMORS CIRCULATED WIDELY IN THE DELHI BAZAARS
FEBRUARY 25 THAT JP NARAYAN HAD BEEN ADMITTED CRITICALLY
ILL OR HAD EVEN DIED IN JASLOK HOSPITAL IN BOMBAY EARLY
THAT MORNING, HOSPITAL OFFICIALS AND JP HIMSELF CLARIFIED
THAT THERE WERE PROBLEMS INVOLVING THE DIALYSIS LINKS
ESTABLISHED FOR NARAYAN AND WHILE NOT SERIOUS, HE WOULD HAVE
TO REMAIN IN THE HOSPITAL FOR THE NEXT THREE WEEKS.
2. ONE SENIOR CORRESPONDENT FOR AN INDIAN NEWSPAPER TOLD
EMBOFF HE HAD HEARD FROM PM'S RESIDENCE THAT MRS. GANDHI HAD
BEEN VERY CONCERNED AT EARLIER REPORT OF NARAYAN'S CONDITION.
HIS SUDDEN DEATH WOULD SET OFF NEW ROUND OF RUMORS AND
SUSPICIONS OF GOVERNMENT INVOLVEMENT IN HIS DEATH WHICH WOULD
DAMAGE CONGRESS ELECTION PROSPECTS.
SCHNEIDER

[Telegram]
Stopping of copper shipments from United States by nations involved in war must inevitably inflict great losses to important Montana industries. It will involve probable closing of Butte mines wherein thousands of men are employed and will affect others engaged in incidental and independent industries. Suffering and privation will result. S. V. Stewart

title: TENERIFE AIR DISASTER - SITUATION REPORT 5
body:
1.  SURVIVORS:  EMBASSY MADRID REPORTS THAT ABOUT 65 PERSONS
HAVE BEEN EVACUATED FROM TENERIFE AND ARE AT THIS MOMENT ON
BOARD USAF C-141 MEDIVAC PLANE DESTINED FOR US.  PLANE
CURRENTLY SCHEDULED TO REFUEL AT MCGUIRE AFB AND PROCEED TO
BROOKE MEDICAL CENTER AT SAN ANTONIO.  OTHERS WILL REQUIRE
HOSPITALIZATION IN SAN ANTONIO OR ELSEWHERE.  2 SURVIVORS
HAVE REMAINED IN THE CANARIES ONE IN CONDITION TOO SERIOUS
TO BE MOVED, ONE IN GOOD CONDITION AT THE REQUEST OF NEXT
OF KIN WHO ARE IN THE CANARIES.
2.  US TEAM:  US CONSULAR AND MEDICAL PERSONNEL CONTINUE
TO ASSIST THE SURVIVORS AND TO ATTEMPT TO IDENTIFY THE
REMAINS OF THOSE KILLED.  INVESTIGATION OF THE CRASH CON-
TINUES.  SPANISH AND DUTCH OFFICIALS HAVE SAID KLM WAS AT
FAULT.  THE KLM PILOT APPARENTLY INITIATED TAKEOFF WITHOUT
CLEARANCE.
3.  TASK FORCE:  EUR AND SCA CONTINUE TO PROVIDE 24-HOUR
STAFFING TO MONITOR AND COORDINATE DEVELOPMENTS.
CHRISTOPHER

All these 5 properties are handsome and substantial. Would seem unlikely they will be left indefinitely in Chinese hands. title: NAMIBIA: TWELVE KILLED IN LANDMINE BLASTS THE RAND DAILY MAIL REPORTED  DECEMBER 12 THAT TWELVE PEOPLE HAD BEEN KILLED DECEMBER 11 IN THE EXPLOSIO
body:
THE RAND DAILY MAIL REPORTED DECEMBER 12 THAT TWELVE
PEOPLE HAD BEEN KILLED DECEMBER 11 IN THE EXPLOSION
OF TWO LANDMINES IN OVAMBOLAND. ACCORDING TO THE
MAIL, THE FIRST INCIDENT OCCURRED AT 0830 AND KILLED
ON MAN INSTANTLY AS WELL AS INJURING FOUR OTHERS.
SEVEN PEOPLE DIED AN HOUR AND A HALF LATER WHEN THEIR
LIGHT COMMERCIAL VEHICLE WAS BLOWN UP ON THE SAME
ROAD. THE MAIL REPORTED THAT, OF THE ELEVEN INJURED
AND TAKEN TO HOSPITAL IN THE TWO INCIDENTS, FOUR
SUBSEQUENTLY DIED. THE NUMBER OF VICTIMS IN THE
EXPLOSIONS HAS BEEN EXCEEDED ONLY ONCE IN NAMIBIA;
IN OCTOBER, SEVENTEEN DIED IN A LANDMIN INCIDENT
ON THE EVE OF THE PRETORIA VISIT OF THE
FIVE WESTERN FOREIGN MINISTERS.
EDMONDSON

1. MIN ECONOMY AND ECONOMIC COOPERATION SHAFEI ANNOUNCED THAT
EGYPT HAD NEGOTIATED $2 BILLION OF CONCESSIONARY CREDITS. AL

CONCERNING SOURCES OF THESE CREDITS.

FINANCIAL AND BANKING CIRCLES DURING RECENT WEEKS CONCERNING THE
NEGOTIATION OF SUBSTANTIAL FOREIGN CREDITS TO EASE EGYPT'S
LIQUIDITY CRUNCH. SHAFEI'S STATEMENT IS FIRST OFFICIAL PUBLIC
INDICATION OF CAMPAIGN'S OSTENSIBLE SUCCESS. THIS STATEMENT
COMBINED WITH PRESISTENT REPORTS OF NEW CREDITS NEGOTIATED
AND RECEIVED WILL REDUCE THE CONCERNS OF MANY OF EGYPT'S SHORT
TERM CREDITORS.

title: The Ambassador in Poland (Biddle) to the Secretary of State
body:
260. 1. In view of (a) increased violence of aerial attacks over Warsaw and (b) turn for worse on northern front whereby German troops have made considerable advance towards Warsaw during past 24 hours, the Polish Government decided early this morning to initiate gradual evacuation of Government offices and foreign diplomatic missions from Warsaw, latter to Naleczow situated 23 kilometers west of Lublin. This adjacent to locality whereto Foreign Minister and staff propose shortly to move.
2. Accordingly, this evening will start evacuating by stages taking confidential codes.
3. Will advise you later of address as to where we can reestablish communications.
4. Military Attache and Harrison remaining in Warsaw at Chancery until final evacuation is ordered of which you will be notified.
Biddle

body:

COUNSELOR APRIL 2 TO INFORM EMBASSY ABOUT (A) TWA'S REQUEST

ENTITIES, IS LOOKING FORWARD TO THE SAG'S EVENTUAL
TAKE-OVER OF ARAMCO WHICH WILL BE RETROACTIVE TO JANUARY
1976 WHENEVER AGREEMENT IS CONSUMMATED.

CONTINUE BAHRAIN SERVICE FOR INSUFFICIENT TRAFFIC IN
ABSENCE SAUDI ARABIA STOP.

title: NIMEIRI'S DISCUSSION OF ERITREAN PROBLEM WITH QAADHAFI SUDANESE  CHARGE' EL AHMEDI TOLD ME MARCH 10 THAT NIMEIRI
body:
SUDANESE CHARGE' EL AHMEDI TOLD ME MARCH 10 THAT NIMEIRI
HAD SOUGHT TO CONVINCE QAADHAFI DURING HIS VISIT IN THE SUDAN
LAST WEEK THAT "THE ARABS SHOULD BE CAREFUL NOT TO LOSE ETHIOPIA
IN THE PROCESS OF PROMOTING ERITREA." HE SAID NIMEIRI HAD
ARGUED THAT THE ARAB STATES COULD BRING ETHIOPIA INTO AN
ANTI-ARAB POSITION OVER A PERIOD OF TIME IF THEY PROVIDED
VIGOROUS SUPPORT TO THE ERITREAN INSURGENTS, AND THAT THIS
IN TURN COULD LEAD TO ANTI-ARAB REACTIONS IN OTHER AFRICAN
STATES WHICH ARE CONCERNED WITH THE ISSUE OF TERRITORIAL
INTEGRITY. ACCORDING TO EL AHMEDI, QAADHAFI ADMITTED THAT
THERE WAS SOME FORCE IN THIS ARGUMENT.
WYMAN

KIVU WITH IACOVOU, UNHCR REP KINSHASA, ANTOINE NOEL, STATED HE
WAS "VERY SATISFIED" WITH THE RAPID INTEGRATION OF ANGOLAN AND

HAD OFFICES IN KIVU, KIMPESE AND MOANDA AND ITS WORK WAS BEING

CONTEXT OF AFRICAN SOLIDARITY, NOEL STRESSED THAT HIS OFFICE WAS
AT THE DISPOSAL OF THE GOZ AND THE PRA TO RESOLVE THE ANGOLAN
REFUGEE PROBLEM IN CONFORMITY WITH THE BRAZZAVILLE ACCORDS.
