title: GOA CONTEMPLATES RECOGNIZING NORTH KOREA
body:
FOLLOWING BRIEFING WHICH RANARD, EA/K, PROVIDED TO WILLIANS,
AUSTRALIAN COUNSELOR, CONCERNING U.S. POSITION REGARDING
KOREAN NORTHWEST COASTAL SITUATION, RANARD WENT ON TO URGE
THAT GOA MOVE CAUTIOUSLY TOWARD RECOGNITION OF NORTH KOREA.
HE RECALLED THAT AUSTRALIA HAD INITIALLY DECIDED TO EXPAND
RELATIONS WITH THE NORTH AS PART OF AN EFFORT TOWARD
BRINGING ABOUT CONTACT BY EASTERN EUROPE AND COMMUNIST
BLOC COUNTRIES WITH SOUTH KOREA.  TO DATE, HE
NOTED, NONE OF THESE COUNTRIES HAD YET ESTABLISHED
RELATIONS WITH SEOUL.  REFERRING TO RECKLESS DIPLOMACY
NORTH KOREA NOW APPEARED TO BE PURSUING WITH RESPECT TO
COASTAL ISLANDS OFF NORTHWEST KOREA, RANARD HOPED THAT
GOA WOULD CONTINUE TO DELAY RECOGNITION OF NORTH KOREA.
KISSINGER

title: The Ambassador in China (Gauss) to the Secretary of State
body:
89. (From Adler to Secretary of the Treasury only). I hear from a most reliable source that: 
 Work is proceeding on only 4 of 7 bases China promised to construct and for which we were to pay. Three bases on which work is not proceeding are much more urgently needed than the others; in fact, delay in their construction will seriously impede war effort this theatre. Reason China is holding up work on them is that we have not committed ourselves to pay for them at official exchange rate.
 In addition China undertook to build other bases for which she is to pay. No work being done on these bases.


Understand White House will be interested in this information which should not be communicated to other sources in view of its delicate character. [Adler.]


Gauss

FOR PROCESSED FURITS AND VEGETABLES WITH HENRIK NETTERSTROM,

title: DPRK threatens to attack ROK over drills (AP)
body:
From: OpsNewsTicker
Sent: Sunday, February 19, 2012 05:30 AM
To: NEWS-Mahogany
Subject: DPRK threatens to attack ROK over drills (AP)


SEOUL (AP) - The Democratic People's Republic of Korea has threatened to attack the Republic of
Korea accusing it of planning live-fire drills near their disputed sea border.
   The DPRK military said the ROK planned artillery drills from five front-line islands off the western coast
Feb 20.
   It says the drills are "reckless military provocation" and the DPRK will launch "merciless" strikes if the
training is implemented.
   The DPRK warned people living on the islands to evacuate before the drills start.

body:
1. RESPONSIBLE MFA OFFICER HAS INFORMED EMBOFF THAT
DENMARK FAVORS AND EXPECTS POSTPONEMENT OF JUNE MEETING.
IN HIS VIEW A JUNE MEETING (OR ANY MEETING PRIOR TO
AGREEMENT ON EC NEGOTIATING MANDATE) WOULD BE FRAUGHT
WITH DIFFICULTIES REGARDING THE PROBLEM OF DETERMINING
WHERE NATIONAL COMPETENCE STOPS AND COMMUNITY RESPONSI-
BILITY BEGINS. OFFICER WOULD NOT SAY THAT EC MEMBERS
WOULD REFUSE TO COME TO A JUNE MEETING, BUT THOUGHT SUCH A
MEETING WOULD BE IMPRACTICAL AND WOULD NOT ACCOMPLISH
MUCH, AS IT COULD COVER ONLY THOSE LIMITED AREAS IN WHICH
COMPETENCE WAS NOT CONTROVERSIAL.  BECAUSE IT IS CLEAR
NOW THAT THE EC WILL NOT BE ABLE TO RESOLVE THE MANDATE
PROBLEM BEFORE SEPT AT THE EARLIEST, THE JUNE MEETING WOULD HAVE TO

WAS RELEASED TO THE PRESS TODAY BY THE NATO PRESS SPOKESMAN:

title: Battle Situation - Noon - 9th September, 1918.
body:
SECRET.

BATTLE SITUATION - NOON - 9th SEPTEMBER, 1918.

1. WESTERN FRONT.

(a) British Front.

On the Somme Front yesterday we took SOYECOURT and our patrols are in VERMAND and VENDELLES and around HESBECOURT. Otherwise no change.

(b) French Front.

Last night the French had taken VAUAILLON south of the river AILETTE.

North of the OISE they hold FARGNIER and QUESSY and have patrols towards LA FERE.

North of the Somme they hold ARTEMPS and LE HAMEL.

2. ITALIAN AND MACEDONIAN FRONTS.

There is nothing to report.



General Staff,

War Office, S.W.1.

9th September, 1918.

Issued at 12.30 p.m.

title: 462. Editorial Note
body: Souvanna Phouma flew to Sam Neua on November 18 for 2 days of discussions with his half-brother Souphanouvong. During these talks Souphanouvong agreed to join a proposed coalition government of national union made up of all factions within Laos including the Pathet Lao and Phoumists with the only qualification being that Phoumi and Boun Oum not serve in the Cabinet. These two, however, could serve in the new government in other non-Cabinet positions. Souvanna wanted the King to call a conference in Luang Prabang to be attended by the leaders of all the Lao factions under a Royal guarantee of safe conduct. He asked Brown to provide an American aircraft to fly a letter to Luang Prabang to the chairman of the King's Council suggesting such a conference. (Telegrams 964 and 968 from Vientiane, November 21; both Department of State, Central Files, 751J.00/11-2160)

INGLY.

title: CZECHOSLOVAK EMBASSY OFFICER ROBBED
body:
1.  VLADIMIR SPINKA, A FIRST SECRETARY AT THE CZECHOSLOVAK
EMBASSY IN WASHINGTON, WAS ROBBED BY FOUR ARMED MEN ON
DECEMBER 15 IN THE VAN NESS CENTER AREA WHERE MANY EMBASSY
PERSONNEL LIVE.  THE INDIVIDUALS TOOK SPINKA'S WALLET CON-
TAINING A SMALL AMOUNT OF CASH, HIS IDENTITY CARDS, AND
SEVERAL CREDIT CARDS BUT DID NOT PHYSICALLY HARM HIM.  THE
IDENTITY DOCUMENTS AND ONE OF THE CREDIT CARDS WERE SUB-
SEQUENTLY RECOVERED.
-   --  - -
2.  THE DEPARTMENT HAS EXPRESSED ITS REGRET TO THE EMBASSY
AND HAS OFFERED ITS ASSISTANCE IN DEALING WITH THE LOCAL
POLICE.  SO FAR THE EMBASSY HAS NOT RAISED THE MATTER
FORMALLY WITH US.  HOWEVER, WE DO NOT RULE OUT THAT RUDE
PRAVO MAY SEIZE ON IT AS ANOTHER INCIDENT OF U.S. OR
WESTERN HARRASSMENT OF CZECHOSLOVAK DIPLOMATS.   VANCE

ACTION IS TAKEN TO CALL ON MOROCCO TO DESIST FROM THE
MARCH.

title: SCHMIDT/ANDREOTTI MEETING
body:
1.  THE FONOFF INFORMS US THAT THE SCHMIDT/ANDREOTTI
MEETING, ORIGINALLY SCHEDULED FOR AUGUST 19 BUT POST-
PONED BECAUSE OF THE KAPPLER AFFAIR, WILL PROBABLY
TAKE PLACE SOMETIME IN OCTOBER.  SCHMIDT AND ANDREOTTI
HAD HOPED TO MEET IN LATE SEPTEMBER BUT WERE UNABLE TO
WORK OUT A MUTUALLY CONVENIENT TIME.  THE MEETING WILL
LIKELY TAKE PLACE IN VERONA.
2.  THE FONOFF DOES NOT EXPECT THE KAPPLER AFFAIR
(SEPTEL FOLLOWS) TO PLAY A SIGNIFICANT ROLE IN DIS-
CUSSIONS, THOUGH IT ANTICIPATES A CONTINUATION OF THE
ITALIAN PRESS CAMPAIGN.  THE PRINCIPAL DISCUSSION TOPICS
ARE EXPECTED TO BE:
-- ECONOMIC QUESTIONS, INCLUDING THE ITALIAN ECONOMIC
SITUATION WHICH THE FRG BELIEVES IS SOMEWHAT IMPROVED;
-- ELECTIONS TO THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT;
-- THE EC EXPANSION, AND;
-- THE ITALIAN DOMESTIC SITUATION.
STOESSEL

title: 293. Telegram From the Department of State to the Embassy in Poland
body:
123. Beam-Wang Talks. Urtel 172 paragraph 2.
FYI. There has been no change in US Navy's normal practice of operating well out in international waters as stated by you to Wang at 82nd meeting. Standard patrol pattern has in fact been even outside 12 mile zone calculated from assumed Chinese Communist base line. No intention here to alter existing patrol patterns.
As noted by you most "serious warnings" in June and July have involved overflights of Paracels. These represent regular reconnaissance patrol which we have conducted for many months without eliciting any protests. ChiCom claims to islands have no status and recent "serious warnings" over them appear to be part of broader Communist effort in West Pacific to force U.S. patrol lines back by threats, claims, protests and occasional attacks. Letter follows. End FYI.
Murphy

Robert A. Lovett

[Telegram]

 
1762. Your 1182, February 24. Much inquiry has failed to show that any order has been issued by the British Government to merchant vessels to arm themselves; but there is reason to believe that the Government has permitted arming when ships have asked. There is no evidence that I have yet found, however, that any transatlantic British merchantmen have been armed. And all the arming that may have been done has been done since the German submarine "blockade" began and it has been done with reference to German submarine attacks.


American Ambassador

title: 438. Telegram From Secretary of State Herter to the Department of State
body:
Cahto 143. For the President from the Secretary.
"Dear Mr. President:
As you will have gathered, we are off to a very slow start. Gromyko's opening speech added nothing and his balking at informal meetings without the presence of the East Germans is likely to slow things down. I have had two good sessions with the Western Foreign Ministers which, while they indicated considerable divergence of views at the beginning, ended with complete agreement since divergence was on tactics rather than principle.
The general feeling here, including Couve de Murville, is that a summit conference some time this fall is inevitable. I wish I could be as optimistic that we will have achieved sufficient progress to allow such a meeting to be held in reasonable atmosphere. I will keep right on plugging.
Faithfully, signed: Chris."
Herter

title: 40. Editorial Note
body: In telegram 139 from Bonn, July 15, Ambassador David K.E. Bruce reported on increasing German anxiety about de Gaulle. Bruce stated that following a period of watchful waiting, responsible German Government and official circles had shown considerable uneasiness during the previous weekend about de Gaulle's ability to restore political health in France and his intimations of a more aggressive and independent French role in NATO. The Ambassador reported that the German press echoed the apprehension about France's future role in Europe. He said the postponement of the proposed meeting of de Gaulle and Adenauer had only encouraged the view that relations between the two countries had worsened. (Department of State, Central Files, 751.13/7-1558)

142. My press telegram 141. Prompt action of Chamber of Deputies in approving declaration of war bill by vote of 62 to 19 bears testimony to effective preparatory work of President. Credit is due also to Serrato who attended entire session lasting from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.
Session was stormy with much irrelevant political debate and insults hurled back and forth due principally to violent Herrerista attack on government. Although President had conferred with Herrerista leaders in hope of inducing conciliatory attitude for dignity of country, Herrerista directorate decided yesterday morning to oppose measure largely on ground of alleged danger of abuse of war powers by government.


Dawson

title: 20. Memorandum From President Johnson to Secretary of Defense McNamara
body:
I would hope that you could develop a new plan for volunteer fighting forces that would proceed with a minimum of overhead and a maximum of energy in direct contact with the Vietnamese at all levels.
I constantly hear, re Vietnam, we have too much staff, too much administration, too much clerical work, too much reporting, too much rotation and not enough action. Taylor and Westmoreland are probably the ablest regulation officers we have but that, apparently, is not all we need from the results we are getting. Much of the trouble may be here in Washington which sets the policy on rotation and reporting and other forms of paper work.
I expect you and Max are right in opposing larger U.S. Forces, but let's develop some alternatives.
LBJ

title: CANCELLATION OF VISIT OF SOVIET MAYORS TO BERLIN
body:
LOCAL PRESS REPORTED OCT 24 THAT, AS INDICATED REF A,
BREMEN MAYOR KOSCHNICK CALLED ON SOVIET AMBASSADOR
FALIN IN BONN EVENING OCT 23 TO SEEK EXPLANATION
FOR LAST-MINUTE CANCELLATION OF VISIT OF GROUP OF
SOVIET MAYORS TO WEST BERLIN. KOSCHNICK REVEALED
AFTERWARDS THAT FALIN JUSTIFIED SOVIET DECISION ON
GROUNDS THAT "INFLUENTIAL CIRCLES IN WEST BERLIN" HAD
SOUGHT TO EXPLOIT VISIT AS DEMONSTRATION OF "BERLIN'S
MEMBERSHIP IN THE FEDERAL REPUBLIC", WHICH, IN
SOVIET VIEW, WOULD HAVE BEEN VIOLATION OF "CLEAR
AGREEMENTS" AS WELL AS OF LETTER AND SPIRIT OF QA.
KOSCHNICK REPORTEDLY REJECTED THIS EXPLANATION AS
"IMPLAUSIBLE" AND MADE CLEAR THAT CANCELLATION OF
VISIT TOUCHED INTERESTS OF STAEDTETAG AS A WHOLE.
HE REQUESTED FALIN TO INFORM HIM AS SOON AS POSSIBLE AS TO
WHEN VISIT COULD BE RESCHEDULED.GEORGE

title: DUTCH MINISTRY DENIES OFFICIAL FRICTION WITH IRAN
body:
1. THE FUROR IN TEHERAN OVER THE PROPOSED AMNESTY
INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE TO BE HELD IN AMSTERDAM HAS DRAWN
LITTLE SPECIFIC COMMENT FROM OFFICIALS IN THE HAGUE. THE
DUTCH ARE PORTRAYING THE AFFAIR AS A PRIVATE MATTER, ONE
WHICH SHOULD CAUSE NO FRICTION BETWEEN THE TWO GOVERNMENTS.
2. MFA COMMENT HAS EMPHASIZED TWO POINTS: 1) THERE HAS
BEEN NO DIPLOMATIC CONTACT BETWEEN THE TWO GOVERNMENTS
ABOUT THE CONFERENCE, AND THE SITUATION THUS DIFFERS FROM
THE 1974 DISPUTE OVER LENIENT TREATMENT OF ANTI-SHAH
RADICALS,WHEN IRAN SENT PROTESTS THROUGH FORMAL DIPLOMATIC
CHANNELS. (NO ONE IN THE MINISTRY HAS SUGGESTED THAT THE
PROPOSED CONSUMER BOYCOTT MIGHT BE OFFICIALLY INSPIRED).
2) THE GOVERNMENT HAS NO LEGAL POWER TO BAN THE
CONFERENCE, SINCE NO PERMIT IS REQUIRED AND SINCE
IRANIAN TOURISTS MAY ENTER THE NETHERLANDS WITHOUT
VISAS.
MCCLOSKEY

title: US-SAUDI COOPERATION: CONSULTATION WITH THIRD PARTIES
body:
1.  ECON/COM MIN INFORMED CABOUAT, CHIEF OF GENERAL
ECONOMIC AFFAIRS, MFA, OF INTENDED JOINT US-SAUDI
ANNOUNCEMENT PURSUANT REFTEL, STRESSING PARTICULARLY
OUR CONTINUED STRONG COMMITMENT TO INTERNATIONAL
COOPERATION IN THE SEARCH FOR SOLUTIONS TO THE ENERGY
PROBLEM.
2. CABOUAT EXPRESSED APPRECIATION ON BEHALF OF GOF FOR
HAVING BEEN GIVEN ADVANCE INFORMATION ON THIS ANNOUNCE-
MENT.  HE EXPRESSED SATISFACTION AT OUR DECISION, SAYING
THAT STRENGTHENING OF OUR BILATERAL RELATIONSHIP WITH
SAUDI ARABIA WOULD ENHANCE STABILITY IN THE MIDDLE EAST
AND WAS THUS IN THE INTEREST OF ALL.  HE SAID THAT
FRANCE'S EFFORTS TO STRENGTHEN ITS BILATERAL RELATION-

body:

ALLY, FINANCIALLY, AND ECONOMICALLY SOUND AND TO SUIT JOR-
DAN'S SOCIAL AND DEVELOPMENT NEEDS AT THIS TIME.   WE

title: The Minister in Egypt (Kirk) to the Secretary of State
body:
1591. Personal for Feis. Is the possibility being explored of extending to Egypt the provisions of the Lend-Lease Act? After all this country is a war theater and I can see large benefits from the political, economic and financial standpoints of developing American-Egyptian relations on those bases not only for the purpose of the actual war effort but also as a possible impetus to a larger postwar trade in this entire area. I have not discussed this matter here but it is also possible that direct dealings between the United States and Egypt in the supply of defense materials might be acceptable to the British as well as to the Egyptians.


Kirk

title: The Chargé in Turkey (Rountree) to the Department of State
body:
confidential 
256. Following my approach Foreign Office pursuant Department telegram 231, Turkish Government again considered question candidacy for SC's and Secretary General discussed matter with me today. He repeated government's concern that unsuccessful overt effort win SC's seat would be embarrassing to government particularly in view early elections. I gathered from conversation that instructions to Sarper mentioned Embassy telegram 189 underlined caution in approaching other delegations.
Secretary General said, however, that he would telegraph Sarper today asking him to consult US delegation to ascertain its present views as to Turk chances of success. If US delegation feels thereby potentially strong support, Sarper will be authorized work in conjunction with US in making preliminary soundings other delegations. Open solicitation of support will follow only if success reasonably assured.
I of course emphasized importance of moving ahead quickly.



Rountree

title: The Acting Secretary of State to the Chairman of the American Delegation (Davis)
body:
9. Your 9, October 25, 4 p.m. is distinctly encouraging. As a clear cut understanding between the British and ourselves in opposition to the Japanese demands seems to offer the only visible chance of effecting their modification, we agree with you that a well-staged, full dress meeting between the two delegations should prove of real value. We assume, however, that when you specify in the last sentence your purpose of "continuing the discussions of last summer" you refer to questions of general principle dealt with in the earlier meetings, notably on June 18 and June 21, and will not allow the discussions  (at this stage at least) to become deflected to technical problems, where existing differences of opinion might be emphasized anew. This could only confuse the picture and encourage the Japanese in their present demands.


Phillips

body:
[Paraphrase]

184. My 181, June 11, 1 p.m. The Foreign Office states that Nelson T. Johnson has been kept informed of Lampson's treaty negotiations, except possibly that C. T. Wang, when he agreed personally to the draft proposal of the Tientsin reservation, was not optimistic at all as to its approval by his Government. Correspondingly, in  agreeing personally to a 10-year duration of the treaty, Lampson pointed out specifically his lack of instructions from his Government on this highly mooted point. The Foreign Office views obviously with concern the status of British residents in the case of the treaty safeguards and the Shanghai reservations being conterminous.
Atherton

SORTIUM MEMBER GENERAL STOKLA, DIRECTOR OF MATERIEL,

SELECTION. WHILE HE WAS UNWILLING TO VENTURE
DATE WHEN CONSORTIUM WILL ACT HE SAID THAT BELGIUM IS
PRESSING HARD FOR EARLY DECISION WHICH DUTCH MILITARY WELCOME.
GOULD

title: CONGRESSIONAL HEARINGS ON DECRIMINALIZATION OF MARIHUANA
body:
1. UPPER VOLTA'S PENAL CODE (SECTIONS 52 TO 55) AND CODE OF PENAL
PROCEDURE (SECTIONS 473 TO 477, AND 699 TO 718) CALL FOR THE
PUNISHMENT OF PERSONS FOUND GUILTY OF POSSESSING OR TRAFFICKING IN
MARIHUANA WITH IMPRISONMENT AND/OR FINES. NORMALLY, A USER
POSSESSING A SMALL AMOUNT IS TO BE IMPRISONED FROM THREE TO SIX
MONTHS, AND A TRAFFICKER IS TO BE IMPRISONED FROM ONE TO FIVE
YEARS. FINES CAN RANGE FROM ABOUT ONE TO TEN THOUSAND DOLLARS.
2. THE DRUG PROBLEM IN UPPER VOLTA IS MINIMAL: THERE ARE USUALLY
NOT MORE MORE THAN TWO OR THREE ARRESTS PER YEAR, AND A FORMER
POLICEMAN WHO WORKED ON DRUG PROBLEMS TOLD US THAT NO PRISON
SENTENCES LONGER THAN SIX MONTHS HAVE BEEN HANDED OUT SINCE ABOUT
1971. GRAHAM

title: 341. Telegram From the Consulate General in Thessaloniki to the Department of State
body:
91. Most significant statement to emerge from three and half hours lunch January 14 with Northern Greek CU leaders at home Bacatselos was measured statement by Deputy Pasmatzides that "unless King terminates favoritism to Caramanlis and returns to neutral role, CU prepared to raise constitutional question and attempt remove both King and Crown Prince from scene". Whether this statement designed as blackmail in obvious hope it will reach King or is advance warning not made clear. In any case circumstances of statement, during deliberate lull in conversation, presence of Bacatselos, Ioannides of Macedonia and CU Deputy Karaghiozis, plus strong emphasis, subsequent reiteration, and reference to "allied favoritism" to Caramanlis, make clear statement not idle theatrics. Indeed appears luncheon was scheduled so statement could be made. Airgram follows.
Folsom

APPARENTLY STATED THAT ROKG "WOULD CONSIDER" DEVELOPMENT OF

title: R/V GYRE RESEARCH
body:
1.  DEPT. HAS CONTACTED DR. PETER BETZER CONCERNING
COLOMBIAN PARTICIPATION IN PROCESSING DATA FROM GYRE
RESEARCH CRUISE.  DR. BETZER REPORTS THAT HE AND
COLOMBIANS, PARRA AND VERNETTE, AGREED THAT COLOMBIANS
WOULD NOT ACTUALLY HELP IN ANALYZING DATA.  DATA RESULTING
FROM ANALYSIS WILL BE PROVIDED TO COLOMBIANS ON FOLLOWING
SCHEDULE:
DECEMBER 1977 - LIGHT SCATTERING DATA
MARCH 1978 - SEDIMENT PARTICLE SIZE DISTRIBUTION
SEPTEMBER 1979 - CHEMISTRY AND MINEROLOGY OF SEDIMENT
MATTER.
2.  APPARENTLY, THE COLOMBIAN PARTICIPANTS DID NOT REQUEST
TO ASSIST IN THE ANALYSIS OF THE DATA AND, THEREFORE, NO
ARRANGEMENTS WERE MADE FOR A MEETING.  EMBASSY IS RE-
QUESTED TO CLARIFY THIS UNDERSTANDING WITH COL. LONDONO
SO THAT IT IS CLEAR WHAT BETZER IS REQUIRED TO PROVIDE.
IF THEIR UNDERSTANDING IS DIFFERENT, PLEASE MAKE THEIR
VIEWS KNOWN TO US AND WE WILL CONFER WITH BETZER TO
RESOLVE THIS MATTER TO THEIR SATISFACTION.   VANCE

title: GUATEMALAN EMBASSY BOMBED AN EXPLOSION OCCURRED NEAR GUATEMALAN  EMBASSY DURING THE DAWN HOURS OF JULY 24. DATT REPORTED THAT THE IMPROVIS
body:
AN EXPLOSION OCCURRED NEAR GUATEMALAN EMBASSY DURING THE DAWN
HOURS OF JULY 24.  DATT REPORTED THAT THE IMPROVISED EXPLOSIVE
DEVICE USED WAS APPARENTLY SIMILAR TO A CLAYMORE MINE AND WAS
PLACED JUST OVER THE WALL SEPARATING GUATEMALAN EMBASSY FROM
THE STREET.  EXPLOSION CAUSED EXTENSIVE PROPERTY DAMAGE
(INCLUDING THE GUATEMALAN AMBASSADOR'S OFFICE) BUT NO INJURIES.
DATT ALSO REPORTED THAT POLICEMAN GUARDING THE ENTRANCE TO
EMBASSY GROUNDS WAS REPORTEDLY LURED AWAY BY A "SERENO" OR
NIGHT WATCHMAN WHO TOLD HIM THAT A FIRE HAD JUST BROKEN OUT
DOWN THE STREET.  FIRST REPORTS INDICATED THAT
LEFTIST REVOLUTIONARY ARMY OF THE PEOPLE (ERP) WAS
GROUP RESPONSIBLE FOR INCIDENT.
DEVINE

title: GOP ATTORNEY GENERALS MEETING WITH UNFDAC EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR
body:
1.  UNFDAC EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR J.G. DE BEUS DID MEET IN NEW YORK
WITH GOP ATTORNEY GENERAL DIAZ POMAR, AS AMBASSADOR VANCE SUG-
GESTED (REFTEL).  UPON HIS RETURN TO PERU, DIAZ POMAR TOLD
EMBASSY NARCOTICS COORDINATOR THAT HE HAD SOUGHT ADDITIONAL
ASSISTANCE FOR PERU FROM UNFDAC.  DE BEUS SUGGESTED THAT PERU

BEUS ALSO SUGGESTED THAT ASSISTANCE TO PERU IN THE NARCOTICS

JAPAN.

DELEGATION FROM LIMA TO THE UNFDAC MEETING IN GENEVA IN
FEBRUARY.  THE GROUP MIGHT BE HEADED BY THE MINISTER OF HEALTH,
ACCOMPANIED BY TWO OTHERS INCLUDING DIAZ POMAR.

title: COFFEE: EXPORT REGISTRATION PRICE
body:
1.  THE BRAZILIAN COFFEE INSTITUTE, IBC, RAISED THE
MINIMUM EXPORT REGISTRATION PRICE FOR GREEN COFFEE FROM US
$1.50 PER POUND TO US $1.60 PER POUND ON AUGUST 25. THIS WILL BE
FOR COFFEE SHIPPED UNTIL NOVEMBER 30.
2.  IN DISCUSSION WITH EMBASSY ECONOFF, FONMIN'S BASIC
PRODUCTS LIAISON OFFICER DAUSTER ARGUED THAT THE REOPENING OF
EXPORT REGISTRATIONS AFTER THE FROST AT THE US $1.50 PER POUND
LEVELS AND THE SUBSEQUENT "MODEST" REGISTRATION PRICE INCREASE
SHOWED THAT BRAZIL IS SERIOUS ABOUT AVOIDING HIGH PRICES WHICH
COULD LEAD TO FURTHER CONSUMPTION DECLINES.  HE ALSO STATED
THAT IN THE FUTURE CHANGES IN THE CONTRIBUTION QUOTA EXPORT TAX WILL
FOLLOW--AND NOT ATTEMPT TO LEAD--THE WORLD MARKET.  ACCORDING
TO DAUSTER, REGISTRATIONS IN THE THREE DAYS AFTER LAST WEEK'S
REOPENING AMOUNTED TO NEARLY 1 MILLION BAGS.
SAYRE

title: TERRORIST ATTACK ON JAPANESE EMBASSY KUWAIT

title: The Minister in Honduras (Summerlin) to the Secretary of State
body:
No. 667
Sir: With reference to the Department's telegram No. 62, July 12, 5 P.M., inquiring what steps, if any, the Government of Honduras has taken to cooperate in making effective in the future the embargo against contraband shipments to Honduras, I have the honor to report that the Minister for Foreign Affairs has stated to me that special instructions have been given to Honduran Consuls in the United States and in Canada, and will be given to the consuls in Mexico, to refuse to issue consular documents for shipments of arms and munitions of war to Honduras without the express authorization of the Government. I am informed also that all Honduran port authorities have been specifically instructed in the matter.
I have [etc.]
George T. Summerlin

title: The Consul at Shanghai (Butrick) to the Secretary of State
body:
820. Reference my 811, August 21, 4 p.m. Rear Admiral Glassford met Vice Admiral Iwamura by appointment at the latter's request this morning. The latter stated that Tokyo is not negotiating with Washington and that the Japanese Foreign Office had requested the American Embassy at Tokyo so to inform Admiral Hart with the request or suggestion that he and Glassford be authorized to continue their conversations. Glassford replied that he was not in receipt of such instructions but that he was willing to carry on purely private conversations if so desired. Iwamura replied that he was representing Admiral Shimada and that he preferred not to begin conversations until Glassford's position was made entirely clear, especially with reference to any present negotiations between Washington and Tokyo.
Sent to the Department and Tokyo. Repeated to Chungking, Peiping, and Tsingtao for the information of Commander-in-Chief. Department please inform Navy Department.
Butrick

title: 188. Message From Premier Kosygin to President Johnson
body:
Dear Mr. President,
According to available information, Israel is ignoring the Resolution of the Security Council, summoning all governments concerned to take as a first step all measures towards an immediate cease-fire and cessation of all military actions in this area.
Such a situation calls for the Security Council to use its authority to guarantee the implementation of its own decision.
In this connection, we have proposed an immediate reconvening of the Security Council to take effective measures for an immediate cessation of military actions and the re-establishment of peace.

282. I have been informed on best authority that Mara Racheva, 25-year-old private [secretary] of G. M. Dimitrov while he was Secty Gen of the Agrarian Party and since then private secty of Nikola Petkov, was arrested by the militia on May 24 and died of torture on May 28. Hristo Stratev and Boris Pashev, both prominent supporters of G. M. Dimitrov who were until recently the Agrarian reps on the Natl Committee on the FF, are now being held by the militia. Barnes

PLEADING -- FOR WHICH I APOLOGIZE.

VISIT WOULD BE A GOOD CANDIDATE: (1) LAST OF THE WORLD WAR II
LEADERS STILL LIVING; (2) PROBABLY THE LAST TIME TITO WILL
VISIT THE US. IN SHORT, THE TITO VISIT HAS CERTAIN HISTORICAL

URGE THAT IT BE MADE.

title: 271. Editorial Note
body:
At the 413th Meeting of the National Security Council, July 16, during his intelligence briefing, Allen Dulles informed the Council of continuing Soviet pressures on Iran. According to Gleason's memorandum of the discussion, July 16, Dulles' briefing reads as follows: 
"Mr. Dulles again indicated that developments in Iran deserved to be followed most carefully. He added that the intelligence community was uneasy. The Shah had recently boldly rejected the Soviet demands but as of now does not seem sure where he is going. We are also very concerned, continued Mr. Dulles, at the incessant propaganda pounding that the Soviet radio was giving the Shah. Some of the weaker members of the Shah's entourage are apparently urging some kind of understanding with the Soviets. Meanwhile, leaders of dissident groups have been trying to make contacts with U.S. officials. These efforts have been rebuffed." (Eisenhower Library, Whitman File, NSC Records)

title: EDA REJECTS UNITY WITH THE COMMUNIST PARTY OF THE INTERIOR
body:
1. THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE OF THE UNITED DEMOCRATIC LEFT (EDA)
WOUND UP A TWO-DAY MEETING JULY 11. THE RESOLUTION OF THE
MEETING WAS PUBLISHED JULY 13.
2. THE MOST SIGNIFICANT ASPECT OF THE RESOLUTION WAS ITS
SPECIFIC REJECTION OF "A PROPOSAL BY THE COMMUNIST PARTY OF
THE INTERIOR FOR CLOSER COOPERATION BETWEEN THE TWO PARTIES
WITH THE GOAL OF UNITY". THE RESOLUTION SUGGESTS THAT THE
INTERIOR'S COMMITMENT TO MARXISM/LENINISM AND COMMUNISM
MAKE SUCH A PROPOSAL UNACCEPTABLE TO EDA.
3. COMMENT: THE REJECTION OF THE PROPOSAL FOR UNITY WITH
THE INTERIOR IS SOMETHING OF A SLAP AT PARTY LEADER ILIOU,
A PROPONENT OF SUCH A MOVE, THOUGH ILIOU WAS ALSO GIVEN AN
OFFICIAL VOTE OF CONFIDENCE BY THE MEETING. IT ALSO LEAVES
THE INTERIOR IN THE POSITION OF UNCOMFORTABLE ISOLATION IT IS
TRYING SO HARD TO ESCAPE.
KUBISCH

I discussed with Mr. Hollister over the telephone this morning the situation with regard to the split that has developed between State and ICA over the ICA program in Latin America for the next three years.
Mr. Hollister disagreed with the action taken by Mr. FitzGerald in the Planning Board and agreed with the State position which outlined a tapering off of the grant assistance program during the  next three year period and placing emphasis on expanded activities of loaning agencies such as the Eximbank, IBRD and IFC.
Herbert Hoover, Jr.

title: CHINESE OFFICIAL ON POSSIBLE VIETNAMESE INVASION OF KAMPUCHEA
body:
1. LI PU, DEPUTY DIRECTOR OF THE NEW CHINA NEWS AGENCY,
RECENTLY TOLD A WEST GERMAN EMBOFF (PROTECT SOURCING)
THAT A VIETNAMESE INVASION OF KAMPUCHEA AND THE CAPTURE
OF PHNOM PENH WERE "POSSIBLE". HE INDICATED, HOWEVER,
THAT THIS WOULD ONLY BE THE BEGINNING OF A LONG STRUGGLE.
WHEN ASKED HOW THE PRC WOULD REACT TO A VIETNAMESE INVA-
SION, HE SAID THAT THE PRC WOULD GIVE KAMPUCHEA "ALL THE
HELP IT NEEDED" BUT THE PRC WOULD NOT INTERVENE MILITARILY.
2. THE OFFICIAL ALSO SPECULATED THAT THERE MAY BE DIFFER-
ENCES WITHIN THE VIETNAMESE LEADERSHIP OVER SINO-
VIETNAMESE RELATIONS BUT STATED FLATLY THAT THE
VIETNAMESE WERE UNITED IN THEIR QUEST FOR AN INDO-
CHINA FEDERATION. "HO CHI MINH WAS EVEN IN FAVOR
OF AN INDOCHINA FEDERATION", HE ADDED.
WOODCOCK

"January 14, 4 p.m. Chita. There has been clash between Czechs and troops of Ataman Semenoff at Mysovaya and other points near Lake Baikal. An armored train and about 1,000 men disarmed and held by Czechs.

title: MESSAGE TRAFFIC
body:
1. THE SECRETARY HAS SEVERAL TIMES EXPRESSED HIS CONCERN THAT
CABLES ARE TAKING TOO LONG TO REACH HIM AND OUR MESSAGES ARE
TAKING TOO LONG TO REACH THE DEPARTMENT.  HE ALSO MENTIONED
THE PROBLEM TO LARRY LAST NIGHT.
2. A QUICK SURVEY OF TOSEC TRAFFIC RECEIVED TO DATE SHOWS THAT
OF THE FIRST 250 TOSECS, ONLY 52 REPEAT 52, OR ABOUT 20 PERCENT
WERE NOT SENT IMMEDIATE PRECEDENCE OR HIGHER.  I WOULD GUESS
THAT THIS VERY INFLATED USE OF HIGH PRECEDENCE ON TOSEC
TRAFFIC IS A MAJOR PART OF OUR PROBLEM.  SINCE WE HAVE SET UP
THE NEW DEDICATED CIRCUIT SYSTEM, I DO NOT SEE WHY THE
DEPARTMENT CANNOT EXERCISE MORE CARE IN ASSIGNING PRECEDENCE
TO TOSEC TRAFFIC.  I WOULD THINK WE SHOULD AIM TO REVERSE THE
PERCENTAGES AND HAVE THE MAJORITY OF OUR TRAFFIC MORE
PRIORITY.
4. ANY HELP YOU CAN GIVE WOULD BE MUCH APPRECIATED.
KISSINGER

title: The American Chargé d’Affaires at St. Petersburg to the Secretary of State.
body:
[Telegram--Paraphrase.]

 
Department's October 24, 6 p.m. As requested Russia will take no immediate action toward recognizing the Government of Mexico, but  only after consultation and agreement with other powers. The Minister for Foreign Affairs said: "I consider Mexican question as concerning only the United States. In my opinion the only satisfactory solution is annexation, and this action Russia would see with approval."
I replied that I felt authorized to state that the United States had no such intentions and that nothing was further from the views of the President.
[C. S.] 
Wilson.

title: FURTHER DISSENTION IN CHAD IN ADDITION TO HIS PROBLEMS WITH PRIME  MINSTER HABRE, PRESIDENT MALLOUM IS NOW DRAWING CRITICISM FROM MA
body:
IN ADDITION TO HIS PROBLEMS WITH PRIME MINSTER HABRE,
PRESIDENT MALLOUM IS NOW DRAWING CRITICISM FROM MAYO- KEBBI
REGION AROUND BONGOR IN THE SOUTHWEST.  A TRACT DISTRUBUTED
IN NDJAMENA LATE LAST WEEK CONDEMNED SARA EXPLOITATION
UNDER MALLOUM OF THE AREA.  IT THREATENED SECCESSION FROM CHAD IF
THIS EXPLOITATION WAS NOT STOPPED.  TRACT DID NOT CALL FOR

WITH HIM.  TRIBAL DIVISION BETWEEN THIS REGION

AT THIS CRITICAL TIME. BRADFORD

body:

BASIS FOR A CONFRONTATION IN A SPECIAL WORLD CONFERENCE
THAT IS ENVISAGED IN PARA 6?  HAS TEXT OF RESOLUTION BEEN
CHANGED FROM THAT GIVEN A/AC.166/L.45?  WE WOULD LIKE
CLARIFICATION OF ABOVE BEFORE GIVING VOTING INSTRUCTIONS,
BUT PENDING THAT OUR PRESENT RECOMMENDATION WOULD BE TO
CALL FOR VOTE IN  ECON  COMMITTEE AND VOTE AGAINST.   KISSINGER

title: Statement by the United States and the United Kingdom Groups
body:
top secret
 

Greece

There was a general discussion about the situation in Greece, and about the importance of maintaining the political independence and territorial integrity of the country as an essential factor in Middle Eastern defense. The American group referred to the gravity of the situation in Greece. It pointed out that it might be necessary for both countries to take further steps to strengthen Greece. The American  group also emphasized the importance of the retention of British troops in Greece during the present emergency.
It was the conclusion of both groups that the preservation of the political independence and territorial integrity of Greece was essential to the maintenance of the security of the Eastern Mediterranean and the Middle East.

title: KUWAITI PRESS STORY ON FUTURE OF MIDEASTFOR
body:
1. KUWAIT DAILY NEWSPAPER (AL QABAS, JANUARY 19) CONTAINS AN
ALLEGED EXCLUSIVE REPORT FROM BAHRAIN WHICH ASSERTS THAT THERE
IS A "GENERAL FEELING IN BAHRAINI POLITICAL CIRCLES THAT THE
AGREEMENT FOR NAVAL FACILITIES EXTENDED TO THE US NAVY BY BAHRAIN
WILL NOT BE RENEWED." THE ARTICLE ALLEGES THAT SINCE OCTOBER 1973
THERE HAS BEEN A BAHRAINI INTENTION TO END THE "FACILITIES;" THEY
WILL TERMINATE AT THE END OF THE "EFFECTIVENESS" OF THE BILATERAL
AGREEMENT. THE WRITER ALSO ASSERTS THAT U.S. DIPLOMACY HAS BEGUN
A "FEELING OPERATION" IN THE GULF AREA TO ASCERTAIN WHETHER THE
BAHRAINIS MIGHT BE PERSUADED TO CHANGE THEIR MINDS. "WASHINGTON
PLACES GREAT IMPORTANCE" ON RENEWAL OF THE AGREEMENT,
ACCORDING TO THE ARTICLE.
2. COMMENT: THIS IS THE FIRST LOCAL PRESS COVERAGE OF THIS
MATTER THAT WE HAVE SEEN FOR MANY MONTHS, OTHER THAN SKIMPY
WIRE SERVICE COVERAGE A FEW WEEKS AGO.
MAESTRONE

title: The Ambassador in Italy (Phillips) to the Secretary of State
body:
330. Yesterday after I had read the President's message to the King he asked me to express his cordial thanks to the President and to say that he would of course at once communicate it to his Government. More than that he said he could not say in view of his powers as constitutional sovereign. He assured me that not one person in Italy desired war and he repeated "not one person".
As soon as I had delivered the message the Embassy in Rome handed a copy of it to the Foreign Office inasmuch as it seemed important in view of the fact that the message was being made public in the United States that the Italian Government should be in a position to make it public simultaneously.
Only the late editions of the morning press contain the briefest reference to the message.


Phillips

Respectfully, yours,

J. B. Moore,Acting Secretary.

SINGLE SUBJECT OF IRAN.
HARTMAN

body:
1.  THE FRG FOREIGN OFFICE OFFICIAL IN CHARGE OF
HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE, ZEHENTER, TOLD US THE
BANGLADESH AMBASSADOR IN BONN HAD CALLED ON THE FOREIGN
OFFICE TO REQUEST FRG ASSISTANCE IN MEETING THE
FLOOD EMERGENCY IN BANGLADESH.  THE AMBASSADOR ASKED
FOR ASSISTANCE TOTALLING BETWEEN 50 AND 100 MILLION
DOLLARS.  ZEHENTER SAID THE FRG CABINET WOULD CONSIDER
THEIR REQUEST AT THE NORMAL WEDNESDAY MEETING.  HE
WAS CERTAIN THE FRG WOULD COMMIT A FEW MILLION DMS
BUT IT HAD YET TO DECIDE WHETHER TO TAKE IT FROM
THEIR DEVELOPMENT AID BUDGET OR THEIR HUMANITARIAN
ASSISTANCE BUDGET.  ZEHENTER ALSO MENTIONED THAT THE
UK HAD ESTABLISHED A DISASTER RELIEF TEAM TO LOOK
INTO THE BANGLADESH EMERGENCY.
2.  ZEHENTER REQUESTED THAT WE QUERY WASHINGTON ON
THE USG'S ATTITUDE AND PLAN FOR FLOOD ASSISTANCE AND
ADVISE HIM ASAP SO THAT THE FRG COULD TAKE THE
USG VIEWS INTO CONSIDERATION IN PLANNING THE
FRG'S RESPONSE.
HILLENBRAND

security problems in Vietnam, and one which when completed would significantly

Subject: France's Lagarde formally announces IMF bid (AP)


PARIS (AP) -.French Finance Minister Christine Lagarde has announced she will seek the top job at the
International Monetary Fund.
  Many European countries, including Germany and Britain, have offered their backing to a candidacy by
Lagarde to run the IMF, which provides billions in loans to shore up the world economy.
  Lagarde had been silent about her intentions until Wednesday, when she announced at a press conference that
she wants the job.

title: GATT - EC EXPORT SUBSIDIES ON SUGAR
body:
1.  AT LAST MEETING OF GATT COUNCIL, WHEN EC AGREED TO
ESTABLISHMENT OF GATT PANEL TO HEAR AUSTRALIAN COMPLAINT
UNDER ARTICLE XXIII CONCERNING EC EXPORT SUBSIDIES ON
SUGAR, BRAZILIANS DID NOT JOIN IN COMPLAINT.  WE UNDER-
STAND THAT ONE OF THE MAIN REASONS FOR EC AGREEING BEFORE
MEETING TO AUSTRALIAN TERMS OF REFERENCE WAS TO LIMIT
DEBATE IN COUNCIL AND TO AVOID POSSIBILITY OF OTHER
COUNTRIES JOINING AUSTRALIAN COMPLAINT.  OUR SOURCES
NOW TELL US THAT BRAZIL HAS ASKED FOR SEPARATE CONSULTA-
TIONS WITH THE COMMUNITY CONCERNING THESE SUBSIDIES.
WE EXPECT, BUT HAVE YET BEEN UNABLE TO OBTAIN BRAZILIAN
CONFIRMATION, THAT THESE CONSULTATIONS WILL BE HELD
UNDER ARTICLE XXIII:1 AND THAT BRAZILIAN OBJECTIVE IS
TO BRING ITS OWN COMPLAINT BEFORE THE GATT.  ALL THAT
BRAZILIAN DEL WILL CONFIRM IS THAT THESE CONSULTATIONS
WILL BE HELD IN THE NEAR FUTURE.  SORENSON

title: MEETING WITH ISRAELI REPRESENTATIVE, DECEMBER 4
body:
1. ISRAELI REPRESENTATIVE HERMELIN CALLED ON ME MORNING
DECEMBER 4 TO EXCHANGE VIEWS. HIS ESTIMATE OF LOCAL
SITUATION ACCORDS VERY MUCH WITH OUR OWN AND HE SAYS
HIS LARGE JEWISH COMMUNITY HERE IS TENSE AND PESSIMISTIC.
2. GREATEST CONCCERN AMONG LOCAL JEWS IS THAT IRANIAN
DISSIDENTS MAY BE RECEIVING WEAPONS FROM PLO. HE BELIEVES
IRAQ WOULD REFUSE, FOR ITS OWN SECURITY REASONS, TO
FACILITATE INFILTRATION OF WEAPONS THROUGH ITS TERRITORY.
BUT HE BELIEVES OTHER GULF STATES, SUCH AS KUWAIT AND
BAHRAIN, WHICH MIGHT NOT HAVE SUCH EFFECTIVE
CONTROL OVER ITS TERRITORY AND ITS RESIDENTS, COULD
BECOME CONDUITS FOR PLO WEAPONS.
3. HE HAS NO RPT NO REASON TO BELIVE SOVIETS ARE
ENGAGED IN ARMS SMUGGLING, EITHER DIRECTLY OR THROUGH
AFGHANISTAN. HE TEREFORE CONCLUDES THAT IRAN'S MOST
VULNERABLE FRONTIERS ARE THOSE ALONG THE PERSIAN GULF.
4. BEFORE HIS ASSIGNMENT TO TEHRAN, HERMELIN WAS
SENIOR ISRAELI INTELLIGENCE OFFICIAL.
SULLIVAN

OF SAS AHLGREEN ERIKSEN MENTIONED

FUEL THIS SEASON AS LAST SEASON. THIS CREATES PROBLEMS,

THROUGH NEGOTIATIONS DIRECTLY WITH THE U.S. SUPPLIER.
SAS HAS NOT CALLED UPON THE NORDIC GOVTS FOR
ASSISTANCE IN THIS MATTER, AND AHLGREEN ERIKSEN DID NOT
FORESEE A REQUIREMENT FOR GOVT ACTION AT
THIS TIME.  IF NECESSARY, SUCH ACTION WOULD

title: CLARIFICATION OF OVERFLIGHT VIOLATION BY US AIRCRAFT N-12EK
body:
1. MFA OFFICER TELEPHONED EMBOFF JULY 25 TO STATE THAT
MFA HAD FINALLY RECEIVED RESPONSE FROM GOP CIVAIR AUTHORI-
TIES IN KARACHI AS TO WHY AIRCRAFT N-12EK HAD BEEN ASKED
TO MAKE TECHNICAL LANDING IN KARACHI WHEN FLIGHT OCCURRED
DURING PERIOD GOP HAD ISSUED NOTAM WAIVING LANDING REQUIRE-
MENT.

ALTHOUGH NOTICE RESCINDING ABOVE NOTAM WAS NOT
ISSUED UNTIL FIVE DAYS AFTER OVERFLIGHT OCCURRED, THE GOP CIVAIR
AUTHORITIES HAD REACHED DECISION THAT THERE WAS NO LONGER A
FUEL SHORTAGE PROBLEM(REASON FOR ISSUING NOTAM IN FIRST PLACE)
AND THEREFORE HAD REQUESTED N-12EK TO MAKE LANDING. THE
CIVAIR AUTHORITIES ALSO AGAIN REPEATED THEIR COMPLAINT THAT
N-12EK HAD NOT RESPONDED TO THEIR REPEATED CALLS.
3. COMMENT: MFA OFFICIAL APPEARED UNCOMFORTABLE ABOUT
TRANSMITTING LAME RESPONSE OF CIVAIR AUTHORITIES AND MADE
IT CLEAR THAT REASONING WAS CIVAIR'S AND NOT THAT OF MFA.

title: (C) INDIAN REACTION TO BHUTTO DECISION: LESS A RAY OF HOPE THAN A  FOOTNOTE
body:
1.  (C) ENTIRE TEXT
2.  LIKE MUCH ELSE IN THE BHUTTO SAGA, THE SUPREME COURT'S
MARCH 24 REJECTION OF THE REVIEW PETITION FILED BY THE FORMER
PRIMIN HAS SPARKED A ROUND OF CONFUSION AND SPECULATION, WHICH
CENTERS ON THE COURT'S COMMENTS ON THE EXECUTIVE'S CLEMENCY
PREOGATIVE (REF A).
3.  AS FAR AS WE CAN TELL, THE COURT DID NOT MAKE A FORMAL
"CLEMENCY APPEAL," NOR DID THEY RECOMMEND THAT THE DEATH
PENALTY BE DROPPED. THE JUSTICES SIMPLY NOTED THAT, IN THE
CONTEXT OF THE EXTREMELY LIMITED SCOPE OF THE REVIEW
PETITION HEARING (REF B) MANY OF THE ARGUMENTS MADE BY
BHUTTO'S LAWYER WERE IRRELEVANT AND/OR REPETITIOUS. THE
COURT THEN ADDED THAT, ALTHOUGH THESE ARGUMENTS DID NOT
PROVE THE CASE FOR A FULL REVIEW PETITION HEARING, THEY
"ARE RELEVANT FOR CONSIDERATION" BY THE EXECUTIVE
AS "MITIGATING CIRCUMSTANCES" WHEN, AND IF, A MERCY
APPEAL IS FILED ON BHUTTO'S BEHALF.
CONSTABLE

body:

JAPANESE DEL. THEY VERY CONCERNED RECENT NORTH KOREAN
ENTRY ON THIS FREQUENCY FOR 100 KW STATION AT JONGJU.

FOOTNOTE IS DELETED AND THAT UNLESS CHALLENGED JAPAN LOSSES

title: ELECTIONS 1974: HALF OF BALLOTS COUNTED
body:
1. WITH VOTES FROM ABOUT HALF THE ELECTORAL DISTRICTS COUNTED, AS
OF 6:00 PM SEPTEMBER 4, OFFICIAL ELECTION RETURNS SHOWED GENERAL
SOMOZA'S LIBERAL PARTY (PLN) LEADING BY 361,470 VOTES TO EDMUNDO
PAGUAGA'S CONSERVATIVE PARTY'S 18,209.  APPROXIMATELY 20 TO
1 ADVANTAGE FOR SOMOZA PERSISTS, AND EMBASSY EXPECTS THIS TO
BE THE APPROXIMATE FINAL RATIO.
2. TALLY OF VOTES PRESENTLY BEING TAKEN IS FROM TELEGRAMS SENT
BY THE SOME 2,700 ELECTORAL BOARDS SCATTERED ALL OVER THE
COUNTRY.  AFTER THE FINAL COUNT FROM THE TELEGRAPHICALLY REPORTED
RESULTS IS COMPLETED, THE SUPREME ELECTORAL TRIBUNAL WILL THEN
REVIEW THE ACTUAL BALLOTS WHICH ARE NOW IN THE PROCESS OF BEING
TRANSPORTED TO MANAGUA.  THE FINAL OFFICIAL RESULTS OF THE ELECTION
WILL THEN BE MADE AFTER THAT REVIEW IS COMPLETED.  THIS IS
EXPECTED TO TAKE WEEKS.
SHELTON

title: CENTRALIZATION OF STATE SECTOR OF AGRICULTURE
body:
1. ACCORDING TO THE JUNE 15 CENTRAL PRESS, THE GOP
PRESIDIUM SET UP A CENTRAL BOARD OF STATE AGRICULTURAL
ENTERPRISES THE PREVIOUS DAY TO COORDINATE THE
AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION OF THE STATE FARMS.

WILL BE TO CENTRALIZE THE CONTROL AND ADMINISTRATION
OF THE STATE FARMS AT THE NATIONAL LEVEL. PREVIOUSLY
THEY HAD BEEN ADMINISTERED AT THE WOJEWODZTWO LEVEL.
THERE IS NO INDICATION THAT THIS MEASURE IS DIRECTED
AT THE PRIVATE SECTOR, WHICH STILL INCLUDES 85 PERCENT
OF POLAND'S AGRICULTURAL LAND. THERE IS CONCERN AT THE
UNSATISFACTORY YIELDS OF THE PRIVATE SECTOR, BUT
HIGH POLISH OFFICIALS HAVE TOLD US IN RECENT WEEKS
THAT THEY RECOGNIZE THAT ANY MOVE TOWARDS
COLLECTIVIZATION WOULD PRODUCE A NEGATIVE
REACTION IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR, CAUSING PRODUCTIVITY
TO FALL.
DAVIES

title: TIBET CONVENES PREFECTURE PARTY CONGRESS
body:

IN TIBET WHICH IS THE FIRST FIRM INDICATION THAT DELEGATE
SELECTION FOR THE UPCOMING ELEVENTH PARTY CONGRESS IS
UNDERWAY. AT THE SAME TIME, AT LEAST ONE QUARTER OF CHINA'S
PROVINCES HELD PARTY PLENUMS (REFTEL) THAT MAY HAVE VERY
WELL BEEN IN PREPARATION FOR THE CONVENING OF PROVINCIAL
PARTY CONGRESSES. ACCORDING TO A JULY 6 RADIO BROADCAST
FROM TIBET, THE CHANGTU PREFECTURE HELD ITS SECOND PARTY
CONGRESS FROM JUNE 21 TO 25, ELECTED A PREFECTURAL
COMMITTEE AND "ACCOMPLISHED THE TASKS OF THE CONGRESS AS
PLANNED." ALTHOUGH THE "TASKS" WERE NOT SPECIFIED
IN THE BROADCAST, THEY PROBABLY INCLUDE SELECTION OF
DELEGATES TO ATTEND A TIBETAN PROVINCIAL PARTY
CONGRESS. TO DATE, NONE OF THE PRC'S 29 PROVINCIAL-
LEVEL UNITS ARE KNOWN TO HAVE HELD PARTY CONGRESSES.

body:
[Telegram]

 
1346. Swedish press reports via Berlin that negotiations political and territorial questions resumed to-day. After discussion the land  [Aland Islands] question came up. Kuhlmann said Germany desired consult Baltic peoples and especially Sweden, who although not represented present negotiations, would probably desire to be. That Entente [status] matter of interest to Germany as one of signers of old treaties and first question to be solved was whether Russia or newly recognized Finland had right to settle this. Trotsky said Finland's independence made no change. Kuhlmann said Germany had individual rights in this question emanating from old treaty signed after Crimean war and which would be basis of German demands now. Trotsky reserved answer.



Morris

title: U.S. FISHING VESSEL A.K. STROM
body:
GENEVA 3010
1.  DURING MAY 5 CONVERSATION WITH CONGEN, NAVY LT. JORGE
JARAMILLO SANDOVAL VOLUNTEERED INFORMATION THAT U.S. TUNA
VESSEL A.K. STROM HAD BEEN FISHING IN ECUADOREAN-CLAIMED
WATERS ABOUT TWO WEEKS AGO.  JARAMILLO, WHO IS COMMUNICATIONS
INSTRUCTOR AT SALINAS NAVAL BASE, SAID THAT STROM HAD
BEEN IN RADIO CONTACT WITH ECUADOREAN AUTHORITIES CONCERNING
ACCIDENT AT SEA OF ECUADOREAN VESSEL.  STROM HAD BEEN UNABLE
RENDER ASSISTANCE.
2.  JARAMILLO STATED THAT HE HAD SPOKEN VIA RADIO WITH
STROM MASTER CAPTAIN DAVID RICO, HIS FRIEND FOR FOURTEEN
YEARS, CONCERNING ASSISTANCE IN A VISA CASE REGARDING
A RELATIVE OF JARAMILLO. JARAMILLO SAID THAT
STROM HAD SAILED NORTH ABOUT TEN DAYS AGO BECAUSE TUNA
DEPARTED ECUADOREAN-CLAIMED WATERS ABOUT THAT TIME.
DEWITT

266. The Embassy understands that today's American press carried despatches reporting rumors described as partially confirmed that offer from Germany to act on her own initiative as mediator in the Sino-Japanese conflict might be made public in the next few days.

Repeated to Brussels for American delegation.
Dodd

Messrs. E. Atkins & Co. to Mr. Olney.

Boston, Mass., January 1, 1896.
Dear Sir: We are informed through confidential but reliable source that it is the intention of the Cuban agents in New York to destroy the buildings and machinery at our estate, Soledad, situated near Cienfuegos, Cuba.

title: Mr. West to Mr. Rogers.
body:
Sir: I have to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of the 19th instant, informing me that you were arrested under the "habeas corpus suspension act," and that you are a native-born citizen of the United States.
I regret to say that I would not be justified in taking any measure for your release on the grounds of your citizenship without having evidence thereof in my possession; so that, in order to avail yourself of my services, it will be necessary that you obtain legal proofs of your birth in the United States.
In writing this, I of course assume that you have been in no way implicated in the Fenian movement.
I am, sir, your obedient servant,

WILLIAM B. WEST, United States Consul.

Mr. John H. Rogers,
Mountjoy Prison.

A-115. Reference is made to the Department's Airgram A-58 of March 5, 1946, concerning Nicaragua's arrears in the amount of $86,063.38 in payment of its Export-Import Bank loan. I had a good opportunity to discuss the matter with President Somoza at El Genizaro.
I allowed the President to read Airgram No. A-58. He said: 
 That he and Ambassador Sevilla Sacasa are not trying to link the Export-Import Bank loan to the Pan-American Highway accounts.
 That he only wants Washington to wait a bit until settlement of the Highway accounts is accomplished in the hope that Nicaragua will then be in a better position to meet the obligation.
 That because the audit of the Pan-American Highway accounts had proceeded slowly, he had had to use the money set aside for payment of the Export-Import Bank loan to finance the highway expenditures.

Warren

Prompt Senate Ratification of the Japanese Peace Treaty
I discussed with the President the relation between the ratification of the Japanese Peace Treaty before the Senate and the completion of the administrative agreement. title: IMPACT OF INCREASED OIL PRICES IN CANADA
body:
1. ACCORDING TO PRESS ACCOUNTS ENERGY MINISTER MACDONALD AT
DECEMBER 27 PRESS CONFERENCE SUGGESTED RECENT MIDDLE EAST PRICE
INCREASE WILL WORK OUT AT $4 PER BARREL FOR OIL LANDED AT
MONTREAL AND THAT THIS WOULD TRANSLATE INTO FURTHER TWELVE CENTS
PER GALLON INCREASE IN RETAIL PRICES GASOLINE AND HEATING OIL.
THIS WOULD REPRESENT A DIFFERENCE OF TWENTY CENTS PER GALLON
BETWEEN PRICES AT MONTREAL AND TORONTO, "AN ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE
LEVEL TO LIVE WITH." MACDONALD REPORTEDLY SAID GOVERNMENT
IS ALMOST CERTAIN TO SET UP A SUBSIDY PLAN AND FINANCE
IT BY BOOSTING THE EXPORT TAX ON CRUDE OIL TO $6.50 PER BARREL
ON FEBRUARY 1. HE INDICATED THIS WOULD BE MAJOR QUESTION FOR
FEDERAL-PROVINCIAL ENERGY CONFERENCE WHICH WILL CONVENE IN
JANUARY. MACONDONALD ALSO INDICATED GOC HAS NO PLANS TO
END WELL HEAD PRICE FREEZE IN WESTERN CANADA BEFORE END OF
CURRENT HEATING SEASON.
JOHNSON

Sir: I thank you for your letter of June 9, 1944, regarding the decision of the United Nations War Crimes Commission to establish at Chungking a Far Eastern and Pacific Sub-Commission.
This Government has designated the American Ambassador in Chungking, the Honorable Clarence E. Gauss, to represent it on the Sub-Commission. He will be assisted by the Judge Advocate of the United States Armed Forces in China-Burma-India. It has not yet been decided whether or not he will have a naval assistant.
This Government understands that the Sub-Commission will be an agency of the War Crimes Commission in London and will receive instructions from the Commission in London together with the necessary documentation.
Accept [etc.]


Cordell Hull

845. For Adler from State and Treas. It is thought that a loan for currency stabilization is not possible at this stage, re Embtel 1301, June 14. title: 291. Editorial Note
body:
Secretary Dulles left Washington on October 21 for the Geneva Foreign Ministers Conference. He arrived in Rome at 6 p.m. and for the remainder of that day and part of the following he met with various Italian officials and Ambassador Luce.
Dulles left Italy early in the afternoon of October 23 and arrived at Orly Field outside Paris about 4:30 p.m. He remained in Paris until the afternoon of October 26, holding meetings with NATO officials, British, French, and Federal Republic representatives on the forthcoming Geneva meeting, and the staff of the Embassy in Paris and the United States Representative to the European Regional Organizations.
The documentation that follows presents only the records of the most significant of these discussions.

title: The Secretary of State to the Ambassador in the Soviet Union (Harriman)

1602. Embassy's 2327 June 28, midnight. As you will have seen from the Department's 5111 [1581], June 28, 9 p.m., our Embassy at Ankara has been authorized to support British efforts to persuade the Turks to sever economic and diplomatic relations with the Axis. This step does not preclude pressure on the Turks to go further along the lines of Molotov's proposal to the Turks to enter the war, if it is agreed that this course is militarily desirable in the light of present circumstances. A statement of the current Russian view on this point is awaited with interest.
Steinhardt is expected in Washington about July 3 and will be consulted on the practical aspects of obtaining from Turkey at this time the cooperation which will contribute most effectively to the Allied cause.
Repeated to London and to Ankara


Hull

title: Ambassador Guthrie to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegrams]

 
Embassy's telegram of August 21, 3 p.m. In a recent conversation with the British Ambassador he has informed me that the assurance given me on August twenty-first by the Minister for Foreign Affairs corresponds substantially with the information received by him from the same source. By the details of the uncompleted conventions, however, he was informed that it would be provided that Japan should furnish Russia, free of cost, with approximately one hundred and forty thousand rifles and a quantity of ammunition and that Russia would reduce its tariff on certain articles of Japanese manufacture.
He asserts that the convention has met with the thorough approval of the London authorities. The Foreign Office has not yet replied in writing to the Department's note verbale of August 16, 4 p.m.


Guthrie

30. My telegram No. 14, June 5, 11 [1] p.m. and Cairo's No. 1221, July 13, 9 a.m. In response to British inquiry from Cairo, British Minister and I on July 1st conferred on advisability of mentioning possible denial operations to Saudi Government. We agreed that such mention would create needless alarm and harm standing of United Nations with local government. Mr. Bird opined that recent German advances in Egypt made present time particularly inopportune.
In my opinion no favorable time will occur to mention denial alone though it might be linked with defense in a more palatable phrase such as "maintenance of military detachments, establishment of antiaircraft defenses and other military measures designed to prevent the oil installation from falling into enemy hands".
Cairo has been informed.


Moose

title: The American Ambassador to Russia to the Secretary of State.
body:
No. 129.]
Sir: I have the honor to report that I called to-day upon M. Sazonoff, the minister of foreign affairs.
In connection with Persian matters he confirmed the statement telegraphed to you on December 8, 1911, to the effect that complete personal protection would be given to Mr. Shuster, including, if necessary, an armed escort out of Persia.
He added that Mr. Shuster's selection was particularly disagreeable to Russia, not only on account of his action, but because he is a Jew. I ventured to say that in this at least I thought he was mistaken, but he insisted upon it with great emphasis and ascribed Shuster's interests to this alleged fact. Nevertheless he assured me that Shuster's personal protection by Russia could be absolutely relied upon.
I have, etc.,
Curtis Guild.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs received a telegraphic report from Tokyo dated January 12 as follows:
Noticing that their occupation of Shanhaikwan and their aggression against Chumen did not produce any noticeable reaction in other countries, the Japanese War Department made public on January 11 an interview to the effect that Jehol is the territory of the puppet government in the Three Eastern Provinces, that any move in Jehol will be considered as an aggressive and disturbing measure against the puppet government which calls for suppression in self-defense, and that no other nation will be allowed to interfere with these defensive measures.
These allegations prove conclusively that Japan has definite designs upon Jehol.

body:
1.  BEGIN UNCLASSIFIED. AS FAR AS WE KNOW THE NIGERIAN GOVERNMENT
IS UNINTERESTED IN BARTER AT THIS TIME, PROBABLY BECAUSE IT HAS NO
NEED TO BARTER CRUDE OIL AND COCOA, NIGERIA'S MAJOR EXPORT
COMMODITIES, SINCE CURRENT DEMAND AND PRICES ARE HIGH FOR THESE
TWO COMMODITIES. PRIVATE SECTOR BARTER HAS NOT COME UP IN ANY
SIGNIFICANT MANNER. ANY PRIVATE OFFERS SHOULD BE DEALT WITH
CAREFULLY. END UNCLASSIFIED.
2.  BEGIN LIMITED OFFICIAL USE:
WE HAVE NOT DISCUSSED BARTER WITH THE NIGERIAN GOVERN-
MENT IN ANY DEPTH BUT WITHIN PAST YEAR HAVE EXTENDED TWO
FEELERS ON BARTERING FOR OIL. NEITHER AROUSED ANY INTEREST.
THE SWEDES HAVE BEEN DISCUSSING SALES OF LNG TANKERS AND OTHER
INDUSTRIAL GOODS TO NIGERIA BUT WE DOUBT BARTER IS INVOLVED
AT THIS POINT. NIGERIA IS UNLIKELY TO SHOW MUCH INTEREST IN
BARTER AS LONG AS IT CAN EASILY SELL FOR CASH.
WYMAN

June 13, 1969
Dear Birch:
I, myself, have met with Herbert Hunsaker.
He is, as you note, an able, experienced consultant
in the field of international education. I told
him that it was rather unlikely we would have need
for his services in the near future because we have,
within the last twelve months, doubled the size of
the professional staff in our Education Projects
Department. Also, within the last three months, I
negotiated an arrangement with UNESCO under which
they will supply professional assistance to us.
However, our needs may exceed our capability, and
if they do, we will surely take advantage of
Mr. Hunsaker's experience.
With best wishes,
Sincerely,

FORMER FORMIN FAHMY (WHOSE PROTEGE ELARABY AND SEVERAL

EGYPT MAKE MORE USE OF UN TO FURTHER PEACE PROCESS.

title: Memorandum of Conversation, by the Adviser on Political Relations (Dunn)
body:
The Ambassador of Poland came in this morning to inform the Department that, having seen reports in the press that the new Polish Prime Minister, M. Sikorski, had stated that an appeal would be made to the Poles in the United States and Canada to assist Poland in defense of her territory, and that they might possibly be recruited in the armed forces for that purpose, he, the Ambassador, had immediately cabled to Sikorski that no attempt should be made to recruit Poles in the United States. The Ambassador stated that he had advised his Government that no action should be taken with regard to the Poles in this country which would in any way be contrary to the neutrality of the United States. He wished the Department to be informed of the stand he had taken in this regard.


James Clement Dunn
